In the first piece in this series, I argued Mississippi should welcome the data-center boom. I stand by that argument. But I would not make it honestly without addressing the environmental concerns directly. Conservatives do ourselves no favors when we pretend every environmental concern is imaginary or anti-growth. Some of the concerns are real, and we lose credibility when we refuse to admit it. We are supposed to be the people who can tell the difference between a real problem and a manufactured one. So let me try.
Three concerns matter most: air, water, and the electric grid. A fourth -- sound -- matters in a smaller way that locals near the sites already know about. On each of them, the engineering exists to do this right. We just have to insist on it.
Start with air. xAI's Southaven campus has been operating natural-gas turbines whose emission potential, on paper, includes more than 1,700 tons of nitrogen oxides, 180 tons of fine particulate matter, 500 tons of carbon monoxide, and 19 tons of formaldehyde per year. Those are the numbers in the federal lawsuit pending in the Northern District of Mississippi. Whether the turbines legally require permits is now a federal court dispute. Mississippi DEQ says the units qualify for a temporary-mobile exemption; environmental groups argue federal law overrides that interpretation. A judge will sort that out. But the larger engineering point remains: we already know how to reduce these emissions dramatically. Selective catalytic reduction cuts nitrogen-oxide output by about 90%. Oxidation catalysts cut formaldehyde and carbon monoxide. Better still is using grid power and putting any new generation on a permitted, controlled site instead of running uncontrolled turbines next to a neighborhood. EPA's recently finalized emissions standards for combustion turbines push the industry in that direction as well. Mississippi should too.
Water is next. Memphis sits on the Memphis Sand Aquifer, our drinking water. The concern that hyperscale cooling systems could draw enormous amounts of water from the aquifer is real. The good news is that the cooling industry is moving fast. Closed-loop and direct-to-chip systems can reduce water use by up to 91% compared with old evaporative cooling. Microsoft is piloting a zero-water cooling design at new sites in Phoenix and Wisconsin. xAI and MLGW broke ground last fall on an $80 million greywater facility designed to recycle 13 million gallons per day and save five billion gallons of drinking water annually. None of that is theoretical. We should require it as a condition of operating in Mississippi, not hope for it.
Electric power is where conservatives have the most leverage and the strongest case. Data centers are huge new loads on the grid. If utilities build new substations, transmission lines, and generation capacity for those facilities and then spread the costs across ordinary ratepayers, Mississippi families end up subsidizing trillion-dollar corporations through their utility bills. Mississippi Power has reportedly delayed retiring older coal plants until the mid-2030s in part because of new data-center load. That is a cost. Virginia has already started addressing this problem: a new "GS-5" rate class that requires data-center customers to pay collateral up front and absorb their own grid-upgrade costs. If a data center leaves or scales back operations, ordinary ratepayers are not left holding the bag. Mississippi should adopt the same idea -- and we don't need a federal mandate to do it. Mississippi does not need Congress to solve this. Mississippi does not need Congress to solve this. The Public Service Commission already has the authority to structure rates so ordinary families are not left subsidizing hyperscale data centers.
On sound, the answer is mostly setbacks, equipment selection, and acoustic walls. It's a real quality-of-life issue for neighborhoods near these sites -- anyone who has lived next to a row of running gas turbines knows it is not a small thing -- and it is the easiest of the four concerns to fix. Counties should write reasonable noise standards into the conditional-use approvals they hand out, the same way we already write them for poultry plants and asphalt batch plants. None of this requires a special agency or a federal mandate. It just requires the discipline to set the standards and enforce them.
There is one more piece, which is the question of process. A lot of the heat in Southaven and South Memphis is not really about the engineering -- it is about people feeling that something massive was dropped onto their neighborhood without their being asked. That is a fair complaint. The fix is straightforward: real public hearings before construction, posted air-permit applications with enough lead time for citizens to weigh in, and county-level conditional-use review with real teeth. Conservatives believe in local government for a reason. We should not abandon the principle just because the project is exciting.
There is a temptation in our politics, on both sides, to pick a tribe and accept everything that tribe believes. The progressive who tells me a data center is automatically an act of environmental racism is asking me to ignore the engineering. The conservative who tells me an environmental concern is automatically a left-wing hustle is asking me to ignore my own eyes. I am not willing to do either.
The right answer for Mississippi is the conservative answer, properly understood: require industry to internalize the costs of its own pollution; require it to pay for the public infrastructure it consumes; protect the citizens who were here first; and let the projects stand on their own engineering and their own balance sheets. That is not anti-business. That is how grown-up business works.
In the next piece, I want to talk about the part of this issue that genuinely angers me, which is what Mississippi is paying these companies to come here, and why no real conservative ought to defend those deals.

# **NYC launches "Operation Boomerang" to stop billionaire exodus as Mamdani's tax policies spark wealth flight**
Medallion Financial Corp. founder Andrew Murstein is personally **[contributing $1 million to launch"Operation Boomerang,"](https://substack.com/redirect/db9ae724-28c5-4d07-9920-20e4d08783c0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** a campaign sending New York hot dogs, bagels and Katz's Deli to Florida-based businesses in hopes of luring them back, estimating he'll raise $20-30 million total. The effort comes as Citadel CEO Ken Griffin and Apollo Global Management's Marc Rowan signal plans to expand outside NYC, while insiders reveal a "silent wave" of companies quietly abandoning the city without public announcements over what they describe as an increasingly unwelcoming business climate.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/db9ae724-28c5-4d07-9920-20e4d08783c0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **New York already bleeding wealth before Mamdani took office** : The Empire State lost $660 billion in economic growth over the past decade according to the Committee to Unleash Prosperity, leading all 50 states, while NYC shed 114,000 more residents to other cities than it gained per the Citizens Budget Commission. Texas has overtaken New York in financial sector employment with 519,000 workers versus New York's 507,000, according to Partnership for New York City data, with JPMorgan Chase now employing more people in Texas than New York.
* **Griffin incident sparked panic among business leaders** : Concerns about Mamdani's "tax the rich" platform erupted into alarm after the mayor filmed a social media video using Griffin's $238 million Midtown penthouse as a backdrop--a move Griffin called "creepy"--prompting former mayor Eric Adams to personally lobby Griffin with a message to "Stand your ground." City Hall officials are reportedly seeking ways to soften Mamdani's anti-business rhetoric, with one anonymous corporate executive noting "The problem is Mamdani has not apologized to Griffin, nor has there been an attempt to make peace."

# **Tyler Robinson defense team building death penalty appeal foundation through courtroom motions, says former prosecutor**
Former assistant U.S. attorney Neama Rahmani said that alleged Charlie Kirk assassin Tyler Robinson's attorneys **[are creating potential appellate issues](https://substack.com/redirect/480e2096-c1f1-4029-968c-20d3a0821377?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** in attempt to avoid death row.
"The defense is probably thinking that if they raise these motions, whether it's to exclude cameras in the courtroom or to disqualify the Utah County Attorney's Office, they're creating potential issues on appeal, even if Judge Graf denies those motions," Rahmani said. **"** So if Tyler Robinson is sentenced to death, he may have more arguments that both state and federal appellate judges will be looking at if he is on death row._"_
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/480e2096-c1f1-4029-968c-20d3a0821377?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Defense cites 600,000+ files as justification for six-month delay** : Robinson's legal team requested a minimum half-year postponement after receiving what they described as incomplete and complex discovery materials from prosecutors on March 12, with one forensic biology expert saying she needs six months just to review evidence. Rahmani predicted Graf will likely grant some delay though perhaps not the full requested timeframe, warning that refusing the continuance "creates yet another issue on appeal" since defendants can waive their speedy trial rights.
* **Prosecution argues transparency combats conspiracy theories** : Deputy Utah County Attorney Chad Grunander advocated for allowing cameras during April proceedings, saying "the best antidote for falsehood is the truth in accuracy" and noting conspiracy theories surrounding Kirk's September 2025 assassination require open proceedings for public trust. Defense witness social psychologist Bryan Edelman countered that coverage has been "sensationalized," while prosecutor investigator Cole Christiansen argued media tone "went both ways" with criticism directed at multiple parties including Erika Kirk and Charlie Kirk himself.

National Nurses Week is a time to say thank you. But gratitude is not enough.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/69884a16-ae84-43de-9836-bc074dadee6f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

[Support the Campaign](https://substack.com/redirect/5f63362e-7cee-4d71-98fa-6ee664f7289f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Health care is one of the largest forces in the American economy. In 2024, U.S. health spending reached **$5.3 trillion** , or **18% of GDP**. Yet only about **20 physicians** serve in the 119th Congress -- roughly **4 senators and 16 representatives** out of 535 voting members.
_**That matters because health care policy is often written by people who have never treated a patient, never rounded in a hospital, never relied on nurses during a crisis, and never watched burnout affect patient care in real time.**_
Connecticut knows this problem firsthand.
In 2022, Connecticut had **89,819 licensed registered nurses** , but only **51,514 were actively working** , and only **45,014 were employed in a nursing capacity in Connecticut**. That means having a nursing license does not mean Connecticut has a nurse available at the bedside.
_**Nurses are Aging Out**_
The age picture is also concerning. The Connecticut Center for Nursing Workforce reported that **50% of Connecticut RNs were over age 50** in 2022, while only **11% were ages 20 -29**. That is not just a shortage today -- it is a warning about tomorrow.
_**How about the Burnout?**_
Nationally, nurses are sounding the alarm. Recent nursing workforce reporting found **62% of nurses reported burnout** and **23% were considering leaving the profession**. Hospitals pay for that turnover, but patients pay the deeper price: fewer experienced nurses, more strain on staff, and more risk in the system.
_**What are the sources of Burnout?**_
According to a [Nurse.com study](https://substack.com/redirect/f68fd40d-a86e-44ad-a3fd-63b26820f4dd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), the 5 main contributing factors to burnout are:
1. Dissatisfaction with salary/wage increase policies (63%)
2. Lack of responsive leadership (60%)
3. Unequal work-life balance (54%)
4. Not being heard (54%)
5. Unmanageable workloads (54%)

_**Connecticut cannot afford to treat nurses as an afterthought. Nurses are the backbone of hospitals, clinics, long-term care, home care, emergency rooms, and community health. They see the system from the inside. They know where it breaks. And they deserve representation from leaders who understand medicine from the front line.**_
_**Physician Nurse Cooperation Works**_
**For nearly a decade I served on the Operating Room Committee of the New York Eye and Ear Infirmary. The committee consisted of Physicians, Nurses and Administrators. We all worked together to make the operating rooms ran on time, ran efficiently. Everybody had a voice and everybody respected each other and each other 's opinion. We were a team that were all dedicated to making things work. As a tertiary care hospital we served the entire demographic spectrum of NYC. Despite providing specialty care to a large indigent population we still managed to operate in the black. More of that is needed today. **
This National Nurses Week, the message should be simple:
Thank you to Connecticut's nurses and all of our nurses Nationwide.
_**We see the burnout.
We see the workforce crisis.**_
_**It is time you have a seat at the table in Congress - We need more doctors, nurses, and health care practitioners shaping health care policy in Washington. Healthcare needs to refocus on the patients and the healthcare providers that treat them, rather than bureaucracy.**_
**Nurses, please help put a doctor in the House -- to make some house calls to DC. - Join the movement and spread this message.**

Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. I’ll be the first to admit, I'm not your typical candidate.
You might actually recognize me from TV — and no, not from a campaign ad.
In December 2023, I walked onto the Jeopardy! Champions Wildcard stage as a Marine Corps Intelligence Officer stationed in Stuttgart, Germany. Heading into Final Jeopardy, I had a lead, a category I liked, and a decision to make.
I bet everything...
... and I was right.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-vandenberg [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-vandenberg]
That's how I approach most things in life. You do your homework, you back your judgment, and you don't flinch when the stakes are high.
Right now, the stakes couldn't be higher — and I'm asking you to back me as I take on my next challenge: Running for Congress.
My name is Tyler Vandenberg, and I'm a Democrat running for Congress in California's 6th District. I'm a Harvard Kennedy School graduate, a former Marine officer, and a proud Californian who has spent his career serving this country and our democracy. Now, I’m coming home to fight for it.
Will you chip in $25, $50, or even $100 today to my campaign and Resist Reclaim Rebuild to help us WIN? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-vandenberg]
DONATE TODAY TO HELP WIN THIS RACE! [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-vandenberg]
I didn't come to this decision lightly. After the 2024 election, I watched MAGA Extremists launch attack after attack on everything I love about this state and this country. Cuts to wildland firefighters. Slashing Medicaid. Threatening to sell off our National Forests. Gutting the agencies that keep our communities safe and our air and water clean.
And then there's Kevin Kiley — my opponent, the man currently occupying this seat.
Kiley has recently tried to rebrand himself as an "independent."
Don't believe it for a second.
Kevin Kiley votes with Donald Trump virtually every single time. The independent label is a costume he's trying on because he knows his record is a liability. He's not independent. He's MAGA with crafty branding.
California's 6th deserves better. And I intend to deliver it.
Here's what I'm going to fight for when I get to Congress:
I'm going to fight to make California affordable again. Housing costs are crushing working families across this district. I'll push for real solutions — more housing supply, stronger tenant protections, and federal investment in the infrastructure that makes communities livable. The cost of living isn't a talking point to me. I worked two restaurant jobs just to make rent when I was starting out. I know what it means to hustle just to get by.
I'm going to fight to protect our public lands and our environment. The GOP wants to sell off our National Forests. I want to protect them, fund them, and keep them accessible to every Californian — not just the wealthy few who can afford what comes after privatization. California's wilderness is not for sale.
I'm going to fight to defend Social Security and Medicare. These aren't government handouts — they're promises this country made to working people. I'll oppose any effort to cut, privatize, or undermine them, full stop.
I'm going to fight to protect our neighbors. Immigrants, women, and LGBTQ+ Californians are under assault from this administration. That ends when we flip this seat.
And I'm going to hold MAGA accountable. Not just with speeches — with votes, with investigations, with every tool available to a Member of Congress. The era of consequence-free MAGA corruption has to end somewhere. It can end here.
I spent years in the Marine Corps learning that servant leadership isn't a slogan — it's a discipline. It means showing up, doing the hard work, and putting the people you serve ahead of yourself. That's the kind of congressman I intend to be.
I'm not coming to Washington to build a brand or further my own career.
I'm coming to do the job.
But I need your help to get there. Races like this one don't flip themselves. They flip because people like you decide early that it's worth fighting for — and put their money where their values are.
So, can I count on you to chip in to my campaign TODAY? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-vandenberg]
CHIP IN TO HELP DEMS RETAKE THE HOUSE! [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-vandenberg]
Every dollar goes directly toward building the campaign that beats Kevin Kiley and sends California's 6th a representative who actually works for them.
Let's get to work.
— Tyler Vandenberg

body:
We can move faster and do more to bring down energy costs in Maine.

| | |
---
---
---
Hi Peter -- As I talk with people across Maine, I hear it more and more: life has gotten too expensive.

My top priority as Maine governor will be to implement practical, immediate solutions to make Maine more affordable. We’ve already released plans on two of my biggest priorities: housing and healthcare. Yesterday at Robbins Lumber in Searsmont, I released a plan to**make energy in Maine more affordable.** As energy costs continue to rise, it drives up the prices of everything else. High electricity costs keep us dependent on expensive fossil fuels and our money flows out of state. The costs weigh on Maine families and businesses. **We must move faster and do more to bring down energy costs in Maine.** My plan focuses on four actions:
* Right-sizing utility profits to lower delivery costs
* Lowering energy costs for manufacturers and Maine’s heritage industries
* Increasing efficiency and saving energy
* Creating a new Maine Generation Authority to power Maine’s future

[The details matter. Read my full plan here. ](https://www.supportrickbennett.com/r?u=gbTKlsDTP6xWO2908dmfEDyaMdDQ7esxCA3vZIOo4k1Iziun55uTopUQrmFabn60j7cTK2GpATeSkQpE-uPWolgX6qBqP52RLR8C0M5bZoBR94Bx6kD2pa_5jV2gjlYDheL-Xedl7HX4ohKu_tZCqSgAYsiDBGbH7gjQqDCexLpkDwZmiM3sMX6CGzEUU8Ct&e=939e09e235be96b0bea768d960703804&utm_source=bennettforgovernor&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=energy&n=1)

Maine has always been defined by people who show up, figure things out, and take care of one another.

Let’s get to work. Rick Bennett

This past week, I spent four incredible days in sunny L.A. at the Milken Institute Global Conference. Held at the Beverly Hilton, the 5,000-person conference brought together the brightest minds in health care, finance, technology, media, defense, and geopolitics. The guest list rivals that of the Met Gala. Speakers included Tom Brady, Governor Gretchen Whitmer, Shaquille O'Neal, Tiffany Haddish, Jill Biden, Admiral (Ret) Bill McRaven, and over 900 more spread across more than 200 sessions. Oh, and me and these great Americans in the pic below.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/543db98b-fe13-4007-bd28-ea0c876ad87b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
On Wednesday morning, I had the privilege of moderating a panel that I will modestly -- or perhaps immodestly -- describe as the best one there - tackling the issue of why half the veterans from WWII started their own businesses, creating iconic global brands like Lowe's, Nike, and Walmart, yet only 5% of our generation of Post 9/11 are doing the same.
The main culprit is access to capital for veteran entrepreneurs.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/bee7a1fb-c877-4d97-bffa-8d2edb0e8477?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
After World War II, sixteen million men came home from the most destructive war in human history and built the American economy -- but today, fewer than 5% of Iraq and Afghanistan veterans start businesses.
That collapse didn't happen because this generation is less capable. It's happened in part because the social fabric that connected people across different socioeconomic lines has disappeared.
There are 1.65 million veteran-owned businesses in this country generating nearly a trillion dollars in annual revenue, and the newest [Milken research report](https://substack.com/redirect/cdc7ed08-58e7-469e-ac6e-8103ff52abb5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), led by Rachel Riley and her team, describes how 60% of veterans who apply for capital still receive less than they need. Twenty-four percent are denied outright, even when they meet the lending requirements. All this while veterans carry the lowest SBA default rates of any borrower demographic and are nearly twice as likely to succeed in small business as their civilian peers.
During the panel discussion, we talked about why America's best-trained leaders are still struggling to access the opportunities waiting for them in civilian life. Here are the 5 biggest lessons from the Milken panel.
This newsletter exists because veterans' stories deserve to be told. If that mission matters to you, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..keZQxx5bE7m7UUWAt5_bLrk2DQkCThvmpENMYwrcNZI?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=196905297)
# **1\. Your Network Is Your Net Worth**
I repeat this mantra so much, I sound like a broken record. You can have drive, smarts, and ambition, but if you don't have capable people around you who can support your vision to open doors or give you salient advice, your opportunities for success are limited.
Few people embody this reality better than Blake Hall, the founder of[ ID.me](https://substack.com/redirect/288821c3-d592-4ebf-8345-256a733b8e03?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Hall spoke about a problem many veterans face after leaving the military: they have the leadership skills, but often lack the social networks that help businesses (or careers in general) get off the ground.
"If you look at World War I, World War II, Vietnam - one of the unintended consequences is that you had social networks forming across economic classes. You had rich kids from Manhattan and a basic training platoon with poor kids from Mississippi and sharecroppers. And when those guys need to start a business, they knew who to call because they had a friend and that friend understood what the military does in terms of leadership. Right now, there's a big gap you don't have. You have the leadership training, you have the skill, you don't have the social network."
Hall was candid about how much luck shaped his own success. He had a colonel who essentially highly encouraged (aka forced) him to apply to Harvard Business School by threatening not to write his recommendation letter.
That decision changed his life.
At Harvard, a classmate wrote him a check for $80,000 before he even knew what he was doing. That classmate then introduced him to David Tisch, whose family owns the Giants and the Loews Hotels, and who was the first Managing Director of TechStars New York. One introduction led to another, and the network that followed turned $40 million in capital into a $1.5+ billion company.
"There are a lot more people like me out there," he said.
"When entrepreneurs are ready to go, if they can pick up the phone and have somebody who can basically be a router to people with capital, that changes lives."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f23445b8-dda9-4f2d-b692-89e23e71a395?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
## **2\. You Don 't Need To Start From Scratch **
Most of the education aimed at veteran entrepreneurs pushes startups. Patrick Flood's problem with that comes down to the success rate -- startups fail at higher rates than established businesses, and most veterans were being encouraged to self-fund through bootstrapping or draining their TSP accounts, the military equivalent of a 401(k), to do it.
Flood built Owners in Honor around an alternative path called entrepreneurship through acquisition, or ETA. Instead of starting a company from scratch, you buy one that already exists with customers and cash flow and you run it and make profits. It could be as simple as buying a laundromat.
Three million businesses are turning over in the next decade as Baby Boomers age out, and there aren't enough buyers to absorb them. Flood believes veterans are uniquely positioned to fill that gap.
"Veterans are best suited because they are courageous, curious, and humble. The best business schools in the country are still trying to do what the military has already done."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/7e895a8b-af58-4c69-89f5-933ebe8dba8f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
### **3\. Corporate America Needs Veteran Mentorship**
Since retiring from the United States Air Force after helping lead 684K airmen and their families, most of the speaking invitations former Chief Master Sergeant JoAnne Bass receives have come from industries trying to better understand geopolitics and national security.
But Bass believes corporate America should be asking a different question entirely: not just how global instability affects business, but why more companies aren't recruiting veterans into leadership roles.
"Nobody develops and builds leaders like the U.S. military- it doesn't matter what branch they're in...it is the strongest leadership pipeline in America," she said.
"No other organization in the world-you can name any organization-develops 100% of their workforce, but the military does."
Jo says the problem isn't that veterans lack the skills corporate America needs. It's that corporate America often doesn't understand the talent pool it's sitting on. Veterans don't need charity or symbolic appreciation. They need an on-ramp -- access to networks, mentorship, and opportunities that many civilians take for granted.
Only about one percent of Americans serve in the military, with roughly 200,000 transitioning out every year. That's an untapped talent pool that's being ignored.
"Our veterans are America's strategic advantage."
She told us the Air Force has an internal document, more than fifty pages long, tracking veterans who left military service and went on to thrive in corporate America.
That's the story we need to start telling.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/79002da2-e1f3-4269-b336-cb191380841a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
## **4\. Get in the Room With Non-Veterans**
Blake Hogan believes the network you don't have is more valuable than the one you do.
Blake Hall proved it as described above -- the network that mattered wasn't other veterans, it was a Harvard classmate who knew David Tisch. That's where everything changed.
The civilian in the room with capital is the missing piece for veterans seeking to start businesses. Courage to walk into unfamiliar rooms, pitch to people who don't share your background, and reframe yourself as an investment opportunity rather than a charity case is a big part of the path to success.
Blake Hogan talked about building veteran entrepreneurship programs across more than 30 cities through Bunker Labs, now part of Syracuse University's Institute for Veterans and Military Families. It started with a Navy veteran, Tom Connor, and he quickly realized two things. "We don't know anybody. We don't have any money." Bunker Labs was built to solve both -- connecting veterans at every stage, from first idea to first dollar to scaling, with the civilian networks they didn't have.
Hogan believes veterans often pitch themselves the wrong way. They present themselves as causes to support instead of assets to invest in. But veteran-led companies are nearly twice as likely to succeed as their civilian counterparts.
Once people realize that, it changes the conversation.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/64f7efcd-73c5-43b3-bb40-ea7fe944a4f4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
### **5\. Stop Waiting For the Perfect Moment to Start**
US Navy veteran John Buckridge manages a $1.3 billion fund at Edgewater and runs Spartan Aerospace Group. He's been investing in veteran-led businesses since day one.
His advice to any veteran thinking about starting or buying a business is simple: don't let what you don't know stop you. "Every marathon runs starts with the first step..lean on the community for some help."

The community, he said, is more accessible than most veterans realize. "If you don't know the guy, you know one guy that knows the guy." He cannot remember a single time he reached out to a fellow veteran for advice and was told no.
John gave a great analogy: when most people see someone down in a ditch struggling to get out, their first instinct would be to throw rope. Veterans do something different. They climb down into the hole with you. Not because they feel obligated, but because they've been there before and they know the way out.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e3a74c00-3c9a-4e0d-b759-32dd4e2b0bf8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* * *
I left Los Angeles more inspired than when I arrived. And it's not just because Tom Brady was walking around the green room by me.
The veteran community is one of the most remarkable networks in this country. It's an incredible strategic asset. We show up for each other no matter what.
It's part of my life's mission to continually build the infrastructure to connect veterans with the right people who can help them build thriving businesses.
If you know a veteran with a business idea, open the door. Be bold. Share your ideas. The community will show up for you.
I'm always happy to be a resource. Find me on [LinkedIn](https://substack.com/redirect/ef2fbe71-a5db-4604-a986-8b972133efef?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), connect, send me a message. Let's build something.

We just got a major update in our work to end gun violence.
#

Friends --
We just got a major update in our work to end gun violence...and it’s not good.
**_FIRST**_ : For nearly 100 years, federal law has banned mailing handguns through the U.S. Postal Service.
**_THEN**_ : Donald Trump’s Department of Justice recently declared they would no longer enforce the ban.

name: Sheriff Joe Arpaio
subject: They charged him with a felony for stopping a riot
body:
Dear Patriot,
They charged a cop with a felony for stopping a riot. I am not making this up.
They want to lock him away for using **non-lethal bean bag rounds** against a violent mob that was blocking an interstate highway, hurling rocks at officers, and bringing Molotov cocktails to the party.
I have seen a lot in my years in law enforcement. I have seen politics poison the justice system. But what is being done to Officer Jeffrey Teng of Austin, Texas is one of the most shameless, stomach-turning betrayals of law enforcement I have ever witnessed.
** [It has to stop — and I need your help to stop it.](http://links.itsourgreatamerica.com/u/click?_t=442fb7cf105f4725a8bda0b6bcffc1bd&_m=573df8b9f1ac454b83b4c495a07712a4&_e=iYoAP-jAU3tb-pVDd7DAWGkx6vAUDh75T4SAkayHlaHAfeuT8Kn9pzY4PQik3ZPNe60ShPzkZOHEuHKiOEeuHOcJzc63tWzkNs9hcIeU0mjj8egcU2cCu6O1Hlov8r7JduaeWjuF8Qkr9rzB9IDlabsH2_cbTDRBmtFFXp44YR_ZuZYLuiq9PqdevrQ_ZGf7-KFEEpa17U-dEI_dhSK4RIpCvfHYcmP98ikaAfnx7fOf1zSHnIyDDVKjdSeGtH8c-O21blmltF5HKaahanB2RZ_7tk46jbBUr8_uq5GksjAbZ-XkUWk0zB90PKYgsf7zRTIcFPgm4hMYYVx2DRM8qM9IEXQmi8syYSIo7RrEmtBbMFzjHXIpZYznnuhbo3NPYpzcUz0cTCmzDBmDTWNFCNNCmLhzemHUU0bjlsapPCJVeA7YOjIwrYd397GPG-qO) **
It was Memorial Day weekend, 2020. Hundreds of protesters flooded the streets of Austin. What started as a demonstration turned into three days of chaos: buildings looted, police vehicles set on fire, a rioter caught with a Molotov cocktail before he could throw it. It took nearly Austin's entire 2,100-officer police force to keep the city from total collapse.
On May 31st, a mob completely shut down I-35 — a major interstate highway — directly in front of police headquarters. Ambulances couldn't get through. Officers gave verbal orders to disperse. A police helicopter broadcast commands over a loudspeaker. The rioters refused.
**Officer Jeffrey Teng and his partner were ordered in to clear the highway.**
Officer Jeffrey Teng with his wife
When they arrived, the mob started throwing rocks. One of those rocks struck Officer Teng's partner square in the chest. Under attack, outnumbered, doing their jobs — Teng and his fellow officers deployed non-lethal rounds to stop the violence.
That's it. That's the "crime."
Now Jeffrey Teng, along with 4 other Austin police officers, faces felony charges. Meanwhile, District Attorney José Garza has dismissed nearly every charge against the actual rioters. The people who threw rocks, set cars on fire, and shut down a highway walk free. The officers who stopped them are being prosecuted.
This is a political vendetta by a DA who has made it his mission to destroy the men and women who keep order in our streets.
And Jeff Teng is paying the price. His career is on hold. His future is uncertain. His trial has been delayed again and again — meaning this family has been living under this cloud for _years_ with no end in sight.
The National Center for Police Defense is standing with Jeff and his family — funding his legal defense and providing support while this ordeal drags on. But we cannot do it without you.
I'm asking you to [ **donate today** ](http://links.itsourgreatamerica.com/u/click?_t=442fb7cf105f4725a8bda0b6bcffc1bd&_m=573df8b9f1ac454b83b4c495a07712a4&_e=iYoAP-jAU3tb-pVDd7DAWGkx6vAUDh75T4SAkayHlaHAfeuT8Kn9pzY4PQik3ZPNe60ShPzkZOHEuHKiOEeuHOcJzc63tWzkNs9hcIeU0mgrStPCo-c5VHm_gX0Nq08_xh3MGacTtLOoowKxuvt5Jru5k_qujvKk9Wa9w0OZHBbDei5yQHOZjtvXh5UkuCYP2ob9T9Yj6ETHvzTTK3k5-1B0nhUUZoucyYb-BtYB2J-Nm_x0puGJQBQ4uYgN37L79J7tv6pUSSUQ7tiqh-WdvRzAR9fZD6cQi3BNxDDIN83QycukJndXNAqNzRLIsy2gYm3CAlgDZm0TnU-pmptgWwKTLSzZops9hx62H7qOw1A1JL8YPk6yHoB_w-fVZFwKEoDSUnLfJL5jLrKBkbxvrTvvspd56V_kgbsZuCqUiRuPoVh4z-tgAkX2Ri4Y-Fi-). $25. $50. $100. | Letter from the Chair
---
Tyranny of the Minority - And the Wisdom of Balance
Dear Nebraska Republicans,
Our Founding Fathers were brilliant. They designed the United States Constitution with a clear purpose: to protect the American people from two deadly threats--tyranny of the majority and tyranny of the minority.
Tyranny of the Majority occurs when a passionate mob or numerical majority tramples the rights, traditions, and freedoms of smaller groups or individuals. The Founders feared this deeply, knowing pure (direct) democracy could lead to mob rule, property seizures, or the oppression of dissenting voices. They countered it with safeguards like the Bill of Rights, the Senate's equal state representation, the Electoral College, and a republic structured to refine and filter raw majority will.
Tyranny of the Minority, by contrast, arises when a small, determined clique--through courts, procedures, or amplified influence--imposes its agenda against the clear wishes of the broader population. This is ruled by obstruction rather than consent.
The genius of the American system lies in its deliberate balance: majority rule tempered by minority protections, and minority rights shielded without granting veto power over the common good. The three branches of government--Legislative, Executive, and Judicial--along with federalism and checks and balances, were engineered to navigate between these twin dangers.
That system has served America well for nearly 250 years. But today, radical activists, activist judges, and fringe voices are exploiting procedural loopholes to impose their agenda on the silent majority. This is tyranny of the minority--and it is happening at the federal level, in Nebraska state government, and even at the organizational level of the Nebraska Republican Party.
Federal Government: Where the Minority Rules
Too often in Washington, a handful of voices override the will of millions:

* Activist Judges: Unelected federal judges routinely block the policies of duly elected Republican presidents and Congresses. One or two judges can halt energy projects, border security measures, or election integrity laws that the American people overwhelmingly support.

* Senatorial Filibuster (Cloture Rule): The 60-vote threshold allows a minority of 41 senators to kill legislation supported by the majority.
* Race-Based Gerrymandering: Recently overturned by the Supreme Courts, some states have drawn districts with race as the primary factor, denying fair representation even where conservative voters form the clear majority.

* We also see the emergence of public opinion surveys being touted as legitimate "polling" to skew legislators' views on issues by misrepresenting the will of the majority.

These tactics let a vocal minority dictate terms to the hardworking majority.
Challenges Closer to Home in Nebraska

* Unicameral Cloture Motion: In our one-house legislature, it takes 33 votes to end debate and pass a bill. A minority of just 17 senators can block the will of the other 32. Nebraska voters keep electing strong Republican majorities--yet minority procedural hurdles keep conservative priorities bottled up.

* Inside the Nebraska Republican Party: Small fringe groups--often with limited actual support--use social media to amplify their voices far beyond their numbers. A handful of disgruntled accounts can dominate conversations and divert attention of leaders from bigger issues.

This distorts our Party's direction and drowns out the reasonable, majority view of Nebraska conservatives who simply want lower taxes, secure borders, and pro-life policies.
A Call to Harmony and Balance
The Founders did not choose between majority rule and minority rights--they sought harmony between them. True republican government thrives when the majority governs with wisdom and restraint, while minorities retain strong protections for their God-given rights.
Let us recommit to that vision. By rejecting both mob rule and minority obstructionism, we can restore a government that truly reflects the will of Nebraska's citizens and America's hardworking families. Together, through principled leadership and civic engagement, we can build a stronger, more united future--one rooted in liberty, fairness, and the timeless promise of e pluribus unum: out of many, one.
In Liberty and in Truth, Mary Jane Truemper Chairman, Nebraska Republican Party

clean_body: News, events, and action items to keep Nebraska red and growing strong. | | | | | | Letter from the Chair Tyranny of the Minority - And the Wisdom of Balance Dear Nebraska Republicans, Our Founding Fathers were brilliant. They designed the United States Constitution with a clear purpose: to protect the American people from two deadly threats--tyranny of the majority and tyranny of the minority. Tyranny of the Majority occurs when a passionate mob or numerical majority tramples the rights, traditions, and freedoms of smaller groups or individuals. The Founders feared this deeply, knowing pure (direct) democracy could lead to mob rule, property seizures, or the oppression of dissenting voices. They countered it with safeguards like the Bill of Rights, the Senate's equal state representation, the Electoral College, and a republic structured to refine and filter raw majority will. Tyranny of the Minority, by contrast, arises when a small, determined clique--through courts, procedures, or amplified influence--imposes its agenda against the clear wishes of the broader population. This is ruled by obstruction rather than consent. The genius of the American system lies in its deliberate balance: majority rule tempered by minority protections, and minority rights shielded without granting veto power over the common good. The three branches of government--Legislative, Executive, and Judicial--along with federalism and checks and balances, were engineered to navigate between these twin dangers. That system has served America well for nearly 250 years. But today, radical activists, activist judges, and fringe voices are exploiting procedural loopholes to impose their agenda on the silent majority. This is tyranny of the minority--and it is happening at the federal level, in Nebraska state government, and even at the organizational level of the Nebraska Republican Party. Federal Government: Where the Minority Rules Too often in Washington, a handful of voices override the will of millions: Activist Judges: Unelected federal judges routinely block the policies of duly elected Republican presidents and Congresses. One or two judges can halt energy projects, border security measures, or election integrity laws that the American people overwhelmingly support. Senatorial Filibuster (Cloture Rule): The 60-vote threshold allows a minority of 41 senators to kill legislation supported by the majority. Race-Based Gerrymandering: Recently overturned by the Supreme Courts, some states have drawn districts with race as the primary factor, denying fair representation even where conservative voters form the clear majority. We also see the emergence of public opinion surveys being touted as legitimate "polling" to skew legislators' views on issues by misrepresenting the will of the majority. These tactics let a vocal minority dictate terms to the hardworking majority. Challenges Closer to Home in Nebraska Unicameral Cloture Motion: In our one-house legislature, it takes 33 votes to end debate and pass a bill. A minority of just 17 senators can block the will of the other 32. Nebraska voters keep electing strong Republican majorities--yet minority procedural hurdles keep conservative priorities bottled up. Inside the Nebraska Republican Party: Small fringe groups--often with limited actual support--use social media to amplify their voices far beyond their numbers. A handful of disgruntled accounts can dominate conversations and divert attention of leaders from bigger issues. This distorts our Party's direction and drowns out the reasonable, majority view of Nebraska conservatives who simply want lower taxes, secure borders, and pro-life policies. A Call to Harmony and Balance The Founders did not choose between majority rule and minority rights--they sought harmony between them. True republican government thrives when the majority governs with wisdom and restraint, while minorities retain strong protections for their God-given rights. Let us recommit to that vision. By rejecting both mob rule and minority obstructionism, we can restore a government that truly reflects the will of Nebraska's citizens and America's hardworking families. Together, through principled leadership and civic engagement, we can build a stronger, more united future--one rooted in liberty, fairness, and the timeless promise of e pluribus unum: out of many, one. In Liberty and in Truth, Mary Jane Truemper Chairman, Nebraska Republican Party Follow us: == | ==| ==| == Donate today: Support the NEGOP at == For more information, visit == | From the Campaign of Senator Pete Ricketts... The National Cattlemen's Beef Association backed our bill immediately. Americans deserve to know exactly what they're putting in their grocery cart. name: Stasha Rhodes, United for Democracy
subject: BREAKING: Senators will question Supreme Court Justices for the first time in years
disclaimer_text: Paid for by United for Democracy
body:
| |
---
For the first time in years, Supreme Court justices are set to appear before Congress. This announcement comes just days after the Court’s decision in _Louisiana v. Callais_ , a ruling that is already making it harder for millions of Americans to have fair representation. This is a major accountability moment. At a time when families are struggling to afford groceries, gas, housing, and healthcare, Americans are watching the Supreme Court weaken a political system that already feels disconnected from ordinary people’s lives, all while enriching themselves with private jet trips, vacations, and other luxury items provided by their billionaire buddies. The Court has enormous power over our daily lives, but almost never faces meaningful questions about their actions. Now the justices are appearing before senators to request funding from the American people. Congress cannot simply rubberstamp the Court’s budget request without asking hard questions about:
* the Court’s role in weakening fair representation
* growing public distrust in major institutions
* whether our political system still works for ordinary people
* and what reforms are necessary to restore accountability and real representation

Dial**(202) 224-3121** and ask to speak to BOTH of your senators, John Fetterman and David McCormick and tell them to demand answers from the Supreme Court at the May 20 hearing. **When you are connected, here’s what you can say:**
> _“Hi, my name is_** _[NAME],_**_and I’m calling because Supreme Court justices are about to appear before Congress after the Louisiana v. Callais decision, and I want Senator [NAME] to demand real accountability. At a time when people are struggling with rising costs and feeling unheard by government, the Court should not be making it harder for Americans to have a real voice in Congress. We need a political system that actually works for ordinary people, and senators should use this hearing to ask serious questions about accountability, representation, and reform._ _This hearing is a rare opportunity for the public to demand answers from one of the most powerful institutions in our democracy._ _I am urging you not to let it pass quietly.”_
Then, hang up and call **(202) 224-3121** again, and ask to speak to your other Senator. Tell them the same thing. This is the first time in more than decade that a Supreme Court justice has faced questions from Congress. Let’s make sure it counts. Thank you, Stasha Rhodes
United for Democracy

Where else on the planet can a big-city real estate guy and a small-town hillbilly team up to bring down a political machine to become the leader of the free world and his right hand?
The answer is nowhere but the Shining City on a Hill.
But just like President Reagan, I believe in my heart of hearts that freedom is always a generation away from extinction.
So while I'll never forget Election Night 2024, my sights are set squarely on Election Night 2026.
That's because EVERYTHING comes down to the midterm elections. If the Democrats win back control of Congress, everything we've worked so hard for comes to a SCREECHING HALT!
That's why the Democrat Machine is mobilizing earlier, faster, and more powerfully than anyone thought possible. And we're in for a shellacking if we don't get our act together. Why? Because the Democrats are...
- Unleashing swarms of attack ads in every swing district - just like 2024 - Plastering the media with anti-Trump propaganda - just like all last year - Weaponizing the Deep State to undermine us - just par for the course - Suing us in court to hamstring our agenda - just like Joe Biden did - Tracking to rake in a billion (with a "b") dollars - just like Kamala Harris
They're throwing the kitchen sink at us because everyone knows they can't win on the issues. The American People rejected their agenda of open borders, hostility toward cops, divisive DEI programming, transgender activism, and hating the freest country on Earth.
It's a losing message. I know it. You know it. And they know it too.
That's why the Democrats resort to the ugly, gutter-level politics that pits Americans against each other. They divide so they can conquer.
And the only way they win is if too many Conservatives in our movement rest on our laurels.
The so-called "experts" say that the Democrat Party is fired up and MAGA will sit out this election without Donald Trump on the ballot.
I say they're full of it (as usual).
I believe in this movement. Even though it's early, I have faith that Conservatives who really get it will rise to the challenge and stand with us. The folks who remember when the Democrats impeached our President, kicked him off the ballot, and indicted him in court WILL step up when we need them the most.
I'm hoping you fit that bill.
[That’s why I’m teaming up with Majority Leader Steve Scalise for the FINAL TIME this month to ask for your help in our greatest hour of need.](http://links.maga-conservatives.com/u/click?_t=da215d85003f407c964bf56cae76557f&_m=33a47bb11eac48f8b64b9e7889eda70e&_e=_9VWZ6AaWB28MnA3nHqCh8P6VOFzDFlP9hJwji73CfOuWKQMrkaIhzunNz3ysU0Ea_nMP_WejmYGs_p97RRb-uSlgdQBTf84W52qDSGJoHsIuHc4MxEfQvJ-KS_kIGq_MuEeTZm17NL84cENDrDCl4BqTLTSZXPkSqFnUKSj-tti8miMM4Vf-thW0Jm04mUN1H4CNqLphE2GVxXQ7ck_BlgJZk7XXmJ_gMo-Ca500U6gxOx_h-N5-9Sdv9wpv_yYM4-JTmQXC7IE4h3bHWsR37AEOgJ40hoZ2kP6vbjlPVdc-phFgfDii1IUNddUP3FZWtvbjkT83T5T4pNEiuF1Dwc0dwXg02DcOS5_2sq6SEa4w1yohQ0gOVO8IyzUY81_kNWEOLidzdMIdR4EpBGbYX25J34Yzdtwdq6BOiEdYm5JJFPhs00XgAZ1oAcZTjciIaULyVhzFXclXW8a3bbJFTaRuQjw5iBovm_fscoLEGHy4rX37xP3l3ON6-MzVvLtbOhkLAfve6h0Rf3ltZ6Vo1PiGTUcZeKHmwiIA7c3cIdOkCPuC--vVgNCIuunT9RRS51rcCqkly5YdvLTtGDE4h0S6ejZkAxBpFFjBo0tS-VhBnyCwGNzFJqt6Kplkebzc_7p7x0vuIb37dBQB36uvSoLnGBdnb-ERCyGqdjq8C7LBNcDButNcPaEh2BAl1JkFW1O0I-7gpqoyf1hlNmK6LhgRaWqMF4BARSQxGqfkGVKuNko_97bEY-UgkgpAxpr)

### The spotlight is getting brighter on our battleground race
| | [Haley Stevens](https://substack.com/@haleyformi)
---
| May 8
---
| [](https://substack.com/@haleyformi)
---

---
| | | [](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9vcGVuLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9wdWIvaGFsZXlmb3JtaS9wL3VuZGVyLXRocmVlLW1vbnRocy1vdXQ_.QCHFnzsUrFQDp1OULhSdKWA3C22gtM1hyFKkUu4mXeo?&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email)

---

**We are now less than three months out from the Democratic primary.**
That's a big deal.
Yes, I know campaigns can feel long. They can feel noisy. They can feel like they go on forever until suddenly, all at once, they don't.
That's what we're looking at now. This race is no longer some far-off thing on the calendar. It's coming.
Less than three months.
That can sound like a long time, but it's an important marker.
**Because this is the point where everything starts to matter even more in our battleground race.** Every conversation with voters. Every endorsement. Every volunteer. Every phone call. Every dollar. Every person who decides, "You know what? I'm in."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c7b840fe-f74b-47bd-bc90-fecd793883b9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
So with less than three months to go, and the spotlight on Michigan getting brighter, I want to zoom out for a moment and give you a sense of where things stand.
**[The good news? This campaign has momentum.](https://substack.com/redirect/c7b840fe-f74b-47bd-bc90-fecd793883b9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
👉 A recent poll showed us in a statistical tie with MAGA Mike Rogers. And poll after poll has shown that I'm the strongest Democrat to take him on.
👉 Endorsements are continuing to come in, which I'm incredibly humbled by. Former Senator Debbie Stabenow endorsed our campaign, along with numerous labor unions - double my opponents', combined.
That tells me working people are paying attention.
**Folks can tell when I talk about lowering costs, creating jobs, protecting manufacturing, and standing up for Michigan 's workers that it's not just campaign talk. This is my life's work.**
But here is the other side of it: The battle for Senate control runs through Michigan. And Republicans know it.
That's why the Senate Leadership Fund - the GOP's main super PAC - has already committed $45 million in Michigan. 💰
Friend, let me stop for a second and just say: that is A LOT of money to pour into one state. And the GOP is spending it here because they believe they can turn Michigan red.
This is going to be one of the most competitive and expensive Senate races in the country, and we have to be ready.
That's why this moment matters so much. Because with less than three months to go, I need the full support of this grassroots team.
This is the time to get involved.
This is the time to make a plan to vote.
This is the time to tell your friends what's at stake.
**This is the time to decide whether Michigan is going to send a rubber stamp for Donald Trump 's MAGA agenda to the Senate - or whether we're going to build the kind of campaign that can take on his candidate and win.**
This fight won't be easy.
But I believe in us. I believe in Michigan. I believe in our grit, our decency, our determination, and our refusal to be pushed around by Republican billionaires and MAGA super PACs.
So yes, we are less than three months out.
If you've been waiting to get involved, I hope you'll jump in now.
**[And if you're in a position to donate to our campaign, I'd be grateful. Everyone chipping in what they can is what will help us build the kind of campaign that can win this primary, take on Mike Rogers, and keep Michigan blue.](https://substack.com/redirect/c7b840fe-f74b-47bd-bc90-fecd793883b9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/c7b840fe-f74b-47bd-bc90-fecd793883b9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
With grit,
Haley

A personal note from Haley 👋

I'm a lifelong Michigander and the daughter of small-business owners. I've spent my career fighting for Michigan's working families - and now I'm running for the U.S. Senate to keep standing up for the people I love.

But here's the truth: Senate control could come down to Michigan. And Trump and his megadonors know it. That's why they're gearing up to spend tens of millions to defeat me and hand this seat to a MAGA Republican.

I need your help to fight back. This race will be one of the most competitive - and expensive - in the country, and I'm counting on grassroots support to win.

If you're with me, will you chip in today?

clean_body: The spotlight is getting brighter on our battleground race | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more The spotlight is getting brighter on our battleground race | | | May 8 | | | | | | We are now less than three months out from the Democratic primary. That's a big deal. Yes, I know campaigns can feel long. They can feel noisy. They can feel like they go on forever until suddenly, all at once, they don't. That's what we're looking at now. This race is no longer some far-off thing on the calendar. It's coming. Less than three months. That can sound like a long time, but it's an important marker. Because this is the point where everything starts to matter even more in our battleground race. Every conversation with voters. Every endorsement. Every volunteer. Every phone call. Every dollar. Every person who decides, "You know what? I'm in." | | ---|---|--- So with less than three months to go, and the spotlight on Michigan getting brighter, I want to zoom out for a moment and give you a sense of where things stand. 👉 A recent poll showed us in a statistical tie with MAGA Mike Rogers. And poll after poll has shown that I'm the strongest Democrat to take him on. 👉 Endorsements are continuing to come in, which I'm incredibly humbled by. Former Senator Debbie Stabenow endorsed our campaign, along with numerous labor unions - double my opponents', combined. That tells me working people are paying attention. Folks can tell when I talk about lowering costs, creating jobs, protecting manufacturing, and standing up for Michigan 's workers that it's not just campaign talk. This is my life's work. But here is the other side of it: The battle for Senate control runs through Michigan. And Republicans know it. That's why the Senate Leadership Fund - the GOP's main super PAC - has already committed $45 million in Michigan. 💰 Friend, let me stop for a second and just say: that is A LOT of money to pour into one state. And the GOP is spending it here because they believe they can turn Michigan red. This is going to be one of the most competitive and expensive Senate races in the country, and we have to be ready. That's why this moment matters so much. Because with less than three months to go, I need the full support of this grassroots team. This is the time to get involved. This is the time to make a plan to vote. This is the time to tell your friends what's at stake. This is the time to decide whether Michigan is going to send a rubber stamp for Donald Trump 's MAGA agenda to the Senate - or whether we're going to build the kind of campaign that can take on his candidate and win. This fight won't be easy. But I believe in us. I believe in Michigan. I believe in our grit, our decency, our determination, and our refusal to be pushed around by Republican billionaires and MAGA super PACs. So yes, we are less than three months out. If you've been waiting to get involved, I hope you'll jump in now. With grit, Haley A personal note from Haley 👋 I'm a lifelong Michigander and the daughter of small-business owners. I've spent my career fighting for Michigan's working families - and now I'm running for the U.S. Senate to keep standing up for the people I love. But here's the truth: Senate control could come down to Michigan. And Trump and his megadonors know it. That's why they're gearing up to spend tens of millions to defeat me and hand this seat to a MAGA Republican. I need your help to fight back. This race will be one of the most competitive - and expensive - in the country, and I'm counting on grassroots support to win. If you're with me, will you chip in today? Paid for by Haley Stevens for Michigan. | | | (C) 2026 Haley for MI 33717 Woodward Ave #539, Birmingham, MI 48009 ? ?

A solemn act of gratitude and celebratory praise.

* **Speaker Mike Johnson** , the 56th Speaker of the House

### Worship Concert
* **Blessing Offor** , an acclaimed singer-songwriter known for his powerful vocals and soul-pop-gospel style

---

Recounting the major chapters of American history where God's providence, protection, and guidance are visible.
### A Message from President Donald J. Trump
###
### God's Hand in the Founding of a Nation

* **Secretary Pete Hegseth** , a decorated Army veteran and the Secretary of Defense

### Let Freedom Ring

### In the Face of Terror: A Nation at Prayer

### America's Witness to the World

Living testimony demonstrating that God is still at work in the lives of people today.

* **Pastor Jack Graham** , senior pastor of Prestonwood Baptist
* **Aodhan King** , Worship Leader, Songwriter, and Founding Member of the Grammy-nominated Christian music group Hillsong Young & Free

Calling the nation toward renewal by looking ahead to the future.

* **Ben Carson** , a world-renowned pediatric neurosurgeon and former Secretary of Housing and Urban Development

name: Deb Haaland
subject: Add your name in support of my vision for New Mexico!
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR AND AUTHORIZED BY DEB FOR NEW MEXICO**
body:
| | | [](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/134?t=1&akid=9437%2E400544%2E1xjAO2)
---
Friend: In a moment, I'm going to share with you my vision for New Mexico — **_[but first, can I ask you to take 30 seconds to personally endorse my campaign for Governor?](https://act.debhaaland.com/signup/em_mw_202605_endorse_vision?email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=&ask=5&source=jtk676-su-nd&refcode=jtk676-su-nd&t=2&akid=9437%2E400544%2E1xjAO2)_**
| | [Add My Name](https://act.debhaaland.com/signup/em_mw_202605_endorse_vision?email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=&ask=5&source=jtk676-su-nd&refcode=jtk676-su-nd&t=3&akid=9437%2E400544%2E1xjAO2)
---
This message is a bit on the longer side, but because you're invested in the future of New Mexico, I hope you'll take the time to read my plan. **As New Mexico’s next Governor, I will:**
**Build Education That Works for New Mexico by:**
* Ensuring students can read before third grade by identifying literacy challenges early and providing targeted support when children fall behind

* Strengthening early literacy screening, expanding bilingual and reading instruction, and investing in summer reading and after-school programs that reinforce learning beyond the school day

* Bolstering access to universal childcare, because learning begins long before a child enters a classroom

* Directing unspent dollars from the Public School Capital Outlay Fund to modernize and improve school facilities so kids can focus on learning

* Expanding outdoor and place-based learning through my Every Child Outdoor Initiative, giving schools the tools and resources to connect classroom instruction to real-world learning that improves engagement and outcomes

**Support New Mexico Families by:**
* Raising the minimum wage and eliminating predatory junk fees

* Passing Paid Family and Medical Leave so people don’t have to choose between caring for their family and making ends meet

* Increasing the child tax credit to put money back into your pockets

* Creating a statewide tenant bill of rights to make renting more affordable and more transparent

* Creating a Critical Sector Housing Fund for workers in critical sectors — like healthcare, behavioral health, social work, education, and more — to recruit more professionals to New Mexico to address endemic shortages that hold our people back

* Aggressively building more housing, eliminating unnecessary red tape, driving state investment into housing, and shortening the time it takes to build a home — and ensuring those homes are built with New Mexican labor

**Back Small Businesses by:**
* Establishing a permanent Office of Small Business to coordinate development programs, fill gaps left by federal cuts, and provide clear access to grants, capital, and state resources

* Cracking down on predatory lending by requiring full transparency in small-business loan disclosures

* Establishing a New Mexico Economic Growth Trust Fund to stabilize our economy in the face of federal uncertainty

**Fix Our Broken Healthcare System by:**
* Protecting and expanding access to healthcare in every part of New Mexico

* Banning medical debt from being included on credit reports

* Expanding New Mexico’s Health Care Affordability Fund to protect access for those who rely on the state marketplace

* Using budget surpluses to fill Medicaid gaps and hire more guides to help people enroll in and keep their benefits

* Ensuring sustainable funding for rural hospitals and clinics, expanding mobile health clinics, and significantly increasing access to outpatient behavioral and mental health care, including a full-scale effort to deliver mental health and homelessness assistance statewide

**Strengthen Public Safety by:**
* Ensuring that law enforcement has the tools, staffing, and technology they need to do their jobs effectively

* Investing in mental and behavioral healthcare, substance use treatment, rehabilitation, and housing stability

* Expanding violence intervention and prevention programs in schools and communities, building accountability systems that emphasize fairness and trust, and investing in community policing models that supplement traditional police work

* Creating a statewide Department of Community Safety staffed with social workers and counselors so law enforcement can focus on violent crime while people get the help they need

* Requiring ICE agents to clearly identify themselves and prohibiting masks that shield misconduct from accountability

New Mexico deserves steady leadership that’s ready on day one, leadership rooted in firsthand knowledge and experience. But the only way we'll be able to make this vision a reality is with strong grassroots support from people like you.
**I'm aiming to get 10,000 endorsements for my campaign before my midnight deadline to show the grassroots strength behind my vision for New Mexico, and I want you to be one of them._[Will you please take a quick moment to sign on now?](https://act.debhaaland.com/signup/em_mw_202605_endorse_vision?email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=&ask=5&source=jtk676-su-nd&refcode=jtk676-su-nd&t=4&akid=9437%2E400544%2E1xjAO2)_**
| | [Add My Name](https://act.debhaaland.com/signup/em_mw_202605_endorse_vision?email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=&ask=5&source=jtk676-su-nd&refcode=jtk676-su-nd&t=5&akid=9437%2E400544%2E1xjAO2)
---
Thank you for your support,

Deb

name: Justin J. Pearson
subject: About Tennessee's districts
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Justice Democrats
body:
This is the latest news.
#
Peter, I'm emailing you more motivated than ever before.
**Republicans passed their racist, outrageous gerrymandered districts in Tennessee that eliminate District 9 as the only majority-Black and majority-Democratic district in our state.**
They have cheated their way into a map that favors Republicans, where politicians are picking their voters instead of voters picking their leaders.
We need to call this what it is: **this new map is a political lynching** — an affront to justice and the fight for equality.
My heart aches for my hometown of Memphis, where I was born and raised and where generations of my family are buried.
[](https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260508-1-jp.yxRbaT&refcode=em20260508-37752&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=2&akid=37752%2E1203867%2ER99o3i)
**But I refuse to give in to despair. Don't give up hope, Peter.** The fight still carries on, renewed with urgency as we work to restore the rights that our ancestors marched, prayed, bled, and died for.
**[This righteous fight for our rights has never been more important, to push back against Jim Crow 2.0, to end the corruption that runs rampant and free, to give Black and Brown People a true voice in their democracy. Our fight continues: Will you please split a donation of $5 right away between me and Justice Democrats to stand against authoritarianism?](https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260508-1-jp.yxRbaT&refcode=em20260508-37752&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=3&akid=37752%2E1203867%2ER99o3i)**
**[Contribute $5](https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260508-1-jp.yxRbaT&refcode=em20260508-37752&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=4&akid=37752%2E1203867%2ER99o3i)**
The Supreme Court's ruling in _Louisiana v. Callais_ cleared the path for this, and I'm sure we're going to see the same playbook in other states soon, robbing Black and Brown People of their voting rights.
Republicans have taken the only Black-majority district from us. But I want you to know: No matter what they do, no matter how much they try to break us and make us bend and quit — **we will still be here.**
I'm still going to fight to demonstrate strong leadership in TN, and I hope that you, as a member of this People-powered movement, are still by my side.
This isn't over, and we will not stop until justice rolls down like waters and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream. **[Will you split $5 or more in the next 30 minutes to fight this authoritarian power grab?](https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260508-1-jp.yxRbaT&refcode=em20260508-37752&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=5&akid=37752%2E1203867%2ER99o3i)**
**[Contribute $5](https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260508-1-jp.yxRbaT&refcode=em20260508-37752&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=24&akid=37752%2E1203867%2ER99o3i)**
In Love and Service,
Justin J. Pearson

**[Donate](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/justicedemocrats?refcode=em20260508-37752-footer&t=25&refcode2=37752_1203867_R99o3i&akid=37752%2E1203867%2ER99o3i)**

**SOUTH CAROLINA** Our friends at the **Freedom Caucus Fund** launched a new TV ad supporting the **House Freedom Caucus's Ralph Norman** for Governor of South Carolina.But this is more than just another campaign ad. Chris Anders** decided to respond creatively. Instead of gift cards, Anders and his team offered cash to anyone interested in selling firearms and then worked to connect those firearms with lawful buyers rather than sending them to be destroyed.The response exploded online.After Anders announced the effort on Facebook, the post went viral, generating more than **4.3 million views**. #
Peter —
I’m back on the road barnstorming the state.
Texans deserve a senator who is willing to go anywhere and talk to anyone.
Like you, I am tired of politicians who hide behind scripted talking points and slick TV ads bankrolled by billionaires. We deserve leaders willing to show up and listen to our communities.
I’ll never agree with every Texan on every issue. That’s impossible in a state this large and diverse. But you should get to hear where I stand and why.
So we’re on the road doing just that. I’ve put tens of thousands of miles on my truck driving across the state since launching this campaign.

And as you probably can guess, our costs have significantly increased since the start of this unnecessary war with Iran. I know that’s stretched a lot of families’ budgets, which is why I recently called for a suspension of the gas tax to put money back in your pocket.
But the truth is, it’s also going to put a strain on our budget too.
**[So today, if you can afford it, I am asking for your help to stay on the road. Can you make a contribution to help us put gas in the tank? clean_body: Can you spare a minute to let me tell you why it’s paramount that we keep fighters like Mike Carey in Washington? | Fellow Conservative, You’ve known me for a long time. You know that I am a firm believer in small, limited government and the "America First" agenda that puts hardworking families ahead of the DC swamp. You also know that in my world, your word is your bond. Whether I’m fighting in the deep swamp or standing up for our constitutional rights, I follow through on my commitments. It’s a simple concept, but one that the radical Left seems to have abandoned years ago. I’ve seen plenty of people come and go on Capitol Hill. Some are just there to warm a seat, and others—mostly across the aisle—are there for the wrong reasons entirely. But every so often, you meet a true patriot who is there to do the work. Mike Carey is exactly that kind of leader. | Mike isn't just a colleague; he’s a friend and a rock-solid conservative. As a veteran and a devoted family man, Mike understands the stakes of the fight we are in. He has been a critical partner of mine in Washington, working to dismantle the deep state and rein in the reckless spending that has squeezed the pockets of every Ohioan. We cannot afford to lose Mike’s voice in Congress. While the media and the Democrats are pouring millions into Ohio to try and flip his seat, we need to make sure he has the resources to fight back. Peter,

I’m excited to share that I have officially filed to run to represent Washington’s 5th Congressional District in the U.S. House of Representatives.

Because of your support, we headed into filing week in a strong position. We have raised over $300,000 - more than 2X all the other challengers combined - and we are powered overwhelmingly by local grassroots donors, not by national corporate PACs or dark money interests.

body:
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | [|
