| | Hi Peter,
On April 24th, our country lost a dedicated public servant.
Dirk Kempthorne devoted his life to serving others—as Mayor of Boise, U.S. Senator, Governor of Idaho, U.S. Secretary of the Interior, and as a friend and advisor to With Honor Action. Dirk’s sense of duty [guided his support for our Afghan allies](https://withhonor.us16.list-manage.com/track/click?u=80940e6d1b1e08928d721cf8d&id=ada22ea939&e=33f53a5b1a), reflecting his belief that America must stand by those who stood with us.
With Honor Co-Founder & CEO Rye Barcott shared his remembrance of Dirk in the _Idaho State Journal_ — we invite you to read it [here](https://withhonor.us16.list-manage.com/track/click?u=80940e6d1b1e08928d721cf8d&id=734180195b&e=33f53a5b1a).
---
|
---
| |

# **With Honor Action Joins 34 National Veterans Organizations and Bipartisan Members of Congress in Push to Pass Written Informed Consent Act**
---
|
---
| | Last week, With Honor Action joined For Country Caucus Co-Chair **Rep. Don Davis** (D-NC), caucus member **Rep. Tom Barrett** (R-MI), Rep. Gus Bilirakis (R-FL), and the Grunt Style Foundation to call on Congress to act on the bipartisan [**Written Informed Consent Act**](https://withhonor.us16.list-manage.com/track/click?u=80940e6d1b1e08928d721cf8d&id=c430a11842&e=33f53a5b1a).
The bill ensures the VA provides clear, written disclosure of risks before prescribing high-risk medications, giving veterans the information they need to make informed decisions and advocate for their care. Our veterans deserve full transparency, stronger safeguards, and the ability to take control of their own health decisions.
---
|
---
| |

# **Bringing Veterans’ Voices to the Heart of Capitol Hill**
---
[|
---](https://withhonor.us16.list-manage.com/track/click?u=80940e6d1b1e08928d721cf8d&id=62a37862d6&e=33f53a5b1a)
| | Washington works better when veterans are in the room. On April 23, With Honor Action and [HillVets](https://withhonor.us16.list-manage.com/track/click?u=80940e6d1b1e08928d721cf8d&id=97b2ad30f6&e=33f53a5b1a) hosted 13 veteran service organizations on Capitol Hill to bridge the gap between grassroots advocacy and legislative power.
Alongside the nearly 40 veteran legislators of the [**For Country Caucus**](https://withhonor.us16.list-manage.com/track/click?u=80940e6d1b1e08928d721cf8d&id=d50e1ff28f&e=33f53a5b1a) , With Honor Action is committed to amplifying the military veteran voice on national security, national service, and veterans affairs issues. Engaging directly with advocates and strengthening connections with organizations that serve those who served our country in uniform remain cornerstones of our work.
---
|
---
| |

# **Celebrating the Revitalization of America’s Maritime Industrial Base**
---
[|
---](https://withhonor.us16.list-manage.com/track/click?u=80940e6d1b1e08928d721cf8d&id=41008bb966&e=33f53a5b1a)
| | Following a joint hearing on American shipbuilding, With Honor Action hosted a reception to celebrate the revitalization of America’s maritime industrial base.
The U.S. shipbuilding industry has reached a critical turning point. Over the last decade, while China built over 6,700 commercial vessels, the United States produced just 37. It isn’t just a matter of trade; it is a national security priority. To maintain our defense capabilities and protect our economic interests, we must bridge the gap between education and the shipyard. Reinvigorating American shipbuilding is essential to ensuring our country remains competitive and secure on the global stage.
We’re grateful for the leadership of Rep. Trent Kelly (R-MS) and Rep. John Garamendi (D-CA), along with For Country Caucus members **Rep. Jen Kiggans** (R-VA) and **Rep. Salud Carbajal** (D-CA), who have elevated the importance of shipbuilding and the maritime industrial base.
Read With Honor Action’s statement from the hearing [here](https://withhonor.us16.list-manage.com/track/click?u=80940e6d1b1e08928d721cf8d&id=4b2053beda&e=33f53a5b1a).
---
|
---
| |

# **The HERO Act: Ensuring Reliable Childcare for Military Families**
---
[|
---](https://withhonor.us16.list-manage.com/track/click?u=80940e6d1b1e08928d721cf8d&id=3e67976dac&e=33f53a5b1a)
| | With Honor Action is proud to endorse the bipartisan HERO Childcare for Military Families Act, co-led by With Honor Action ally **Senator Joni Ernst** (R-IA) and For Country Caucus member **Rep. Jen Kiggans** (R-VA), which aims to improve access to reliable, high-quality childcare for military families. As of early 2026, approximately 7,800 military children remain on waitlists for spots in Department of Defense Child Development Centers. Learn more about how the HERO Act would bolster military child care [here](https://withhonor.us16.list-manage.com/track/click?u=80940e6d1b1e08928d721cf8d&id=205d7aac43&e=33f53a5b1a).

**" Show me who makes a profit from war, and I'll show you how to stop the war."**
**-- [Henry Ford](https://substack.com/redirect/147437b3-f1a5-49fe-9f7c-04c464c82f70?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
In the shadows of international diplomacy, a multitrillion-dollar network silently shapes global power dynamics. The global arms trade, a labyrinthine system of legal contracts, covert operations, and financial mechanisms, functions as both business and geopolitical control, influencing conflicts far more effectively than treaties or democratic processes. An extensive analysis of the past two decades reveals that weapons flows align almost perfectly with the world's most devastating conflicts, suggesting a calculated system perpetuated by powerful state-corporate alliances.

The international weapons market operates through two interconnected channels. The first--legal trade--officially occurs between states through authorized defense contracts. Despite theoretical oversight by institutions like the UN Register of Conventional Arms, enforcement remains largely ineffective. As of the mid-2020s, the United States dominates this market with approximately 40% of global exports, followed by Russia at 15%, with France, China, and Germany each holding 5-10% market share.
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=6729589&post_id=196802616&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTk2ODAyNjE2LCJpYXQiOjE3NzgyNTk5ODIsImV4cCI6MTc4MDg1MTk4MiwiaXNzIjoicHViLTY3Mjk1ODkiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.xHNHiNWAKVIAWUIaGx45WyA-GL-bZxw2dzF-2QmgOl4)
"The legal arms trade is essentially a controlled illusion," states defense analyst Maria Chen. "While it appears structured and regulated, end-user verification is notoriously unreliable, and weapons routinely disappear from official inventories after delivery."

The second channel--the illicit "gray and black" market--operates through unregistered sales, shell companies, and covert intelligence operations. What makes this particularly disturbing is how frequently it overlaps with legitimate trade channels. Large defense manufacturers and governments often launder their own deals through intermediaries, creating plausible deniability as weapons eventually reach "non-state actors." Africa, Latin America, and the Middle East bear the brunt of these illicit flows.

A handful of colossal corporations--Lockheed Martin, Raytheon Technologies, BAE Systems, Northrop Grumman, Thales, and General Dynamics--dominate the military-industrial complex. These companies wield outsized influence through strategic campaign donations, revolving door employment practices, and funded think tanks that justify perpetual military engagement.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9oZWFydGxhbmRqb3VybmFsLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.3XSssQSA103KxMqsu6DlChpnPBY4Kj3Ar1Q--UrpHRQ?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=196802616)
The result is a self-sustaining feedback loop: fear generates funding, which fuels manufacturing, which creates conditions for conflict, which drives demand, which leads to more funding. Every escalation, every new tension between nations, translates to higher stock prices for these defense giants. Peace, by contrast, hurts the bottom line.

"When Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022, defense stocks surged," notes economist Dr. David Wilson. "Lockheed Martin alone saw a 15% increase in stock value within weeks. The market rewards conflict, and these executives know it."

Our analysis of arms trade routes from 2006-2026 reveals stark patterns emerging around five major exporters. These networks collectively account for 90% of the world's weapons flow, creating almost symmetrical collision points of Atlantic (U.S.-Europe) and Pacific (China-Russia) supplies over Middle Eastern and Eastern European battlegrounds.

The Middle East serves as the world's premier arms marketplace, receiving 40% of global weapons exports. The Arabian Peninsula functions as a distribution funnel--receiving Western weapons and exporting instability to Yemen, Syria, and Libya. Between 2015-2023, U.S. defense contractors delivered over $100 billion in weapons to Gulf states, many deployed in the Yemen intervention that created one of modern history's worst humanitarian crises.

"Every Saudi air raid in Yemen contained components built by Lockheed Martin, Boeing, or Raytheon," reveals investigative journalist Sarah Jensen. "U.S. State Department end-use monitoring existed mostly on paper, with little practical verification of how these weapons were ultimately used."

In Eastern Europe, the Ukraine conflict revived dormant Cold War industry lines. After 2014, vast quantities of second-hand Soviet weaponry were distributed through Czech, Polish, and Bulgarian arms hubs. When Western stocks of "legacy" gear dwindled, contracts with Rheinmetall, BAE, and General Dynamics scaled up dramatically.

Africa has become a shadow network where weapons from every major export bloc circulate among militias, insurgents, and even poaching operations. Small arms, drones, and armored vehicles arrive under "counter-terrorism assistance" labels while perpetuating conflict rather than security.

"The real arms economy extends far beyond contracts--it's intertwined with energy politics, resource control, and covert influence," explains geopolitical analyst Fatima Al-Rashid.

Petrodollar geopolitics maintain the dollar's dominance while recycling oil wealth back into the U.S. defense sector. Saudi Arabia's and UAE's extensive military purchases lock them diplomatically and financially into Washington's sphere. Most arms deals are denominated in U.S. dollars, reinforcing this financial dependency.

"Our analysis shows a clear quid pro quo: Gulf states purchase $20 billion in jets, which buys them political protection and ensures their oil wealth stays within the dollar system," says Al-Rashid. "The arrangement benefits everyone except the civilians living under these authoritarian regimes and the victims of wars fought with these weapons."

Perhaps the most disturbing aspect of the global arms trade involves how humanitarian organizations--wittingly or unwittingly--facilitate weapons transfers. Non-governmental organizations (NGOs), development contractors, and even UN agencies sometimes serve as logistical masks for the transfer of weapons and dual-use equipment.

"In war zones, the same cargo planes, ports, and contractors are used for both aid and military operations," notes security analyst Michael Torres. "Powerful states exploit this overlap, shipping weapon components marked as 'communications equipment' or 'medical supplies' through humanitarian corridors."

This "humanitarian logistics complex" creates an unsettling cycle: defense agencies fund networks that depend on those funds for survival, leading to self-censorship about donor militarism. By 2020, over 60% of large humanitarian funding flowed through governments belonging to the same trade blocs selling weapons to those warzones.

After the bombing of infrastructure, reconstruction contracts often feed the very corporations that produced the destruction. Military debris removal contracts go to defense subcontractors; construction materials come from firms linked to donors' domestic arms suppliers; security for aid convoys comes from private military companies like DynCorp, Amentum, or Wagner. "Peacebuilding" becomes an extension of war commerce.

Every major U.S. or NATO intervention leaves behind uncounted stockpiles that eventually feed new conflicts. The 2021 withdrawal from Afghanistan saw tens of thousands of rifles, drones, and vehicles fall into Taliban control, later resold through Pakistan into Africa. Libya's post-2011 looted Gaddafi arsenal fueled Sahel insurgencies. Since 2022, shipments to Ukraine have begun appearing in black markets across Eastern Europe and the Middle East.

"This is the arms trade equivalent of climate change--a delayed environmental disaster," says migration researcher Dr. Lena Kowalski. "Once military hardware enters a failed state, it doesn't disappear; it metastasizes and circulates for decades, often ending up in completely unrelated conflicts."

These flows largely escape regulation because current arms tracking systems only cover declared military shipments, not "civilian humanitarian logistics." When NGOs subconvey airlift to "defense partners," invoice details remain protected as proprietary information.

Despite institutional inertia, several solutions could break this cycle. Full transparency of defense contracts and foreign arms sales--including cost, destination, and recipient end-use verification--would represent a significant first step. Independent international auditing bodies, not controlled by NATO or major exporters, could investigate compliance without conflicts of interest.

"Economic diversification is crucial for developing nations," says development economist Dr. Hassan Al-Mansur. "Many countries accept these 'security cooperation' deals because they have no alternatives. Creating viable economic pathways beyond military dependency would fundamentally shift these power dynamics."

Public awareness campaigns exposing how much national budgets fuel endless military build-ups rather than domestic well-being could generate political pressure for change. Several European nations have already begun implementing mandatory defense contract disclosures, though American arms traders remain largely exempt from such transparency measures.

The global arms trade functions as the circulatory system of power--feeding both technological progress and mass destruction. As our analysis demonstrates, few major conflicts over the past twenty years have occurred along paths untraceable to formal weapons deliveries. The movement of weapons represents the bloodstream of geopolitics, and those who control the arteries ultimately control history.

"Every bullet has a supply chain, and every supply chain exists with consent from power," summarizes former UN weapons inspector Henrik Larsen. "Until defense industries face genuine public oversight instead of hiding behind 'national security' mystique, humanity remains locked in a war-profit cycle disguised as diplomacy."

Within this system, the humanitarian sector has been co-opted as moral camouflage--a red-cross sticker on the side of the same airplanes that deliver bombs. Without radical transparency and accountability across the entire logistics ecosystem, both weapons and the aid that often accompanies them will continue to create rather than alleviate global suffering.

The evidence is clear: the most effective path toward peace requires treating the supply chain of humanitarian logistics with the same scrutiny as nuclear material--tracked, verified, and audited publicly. Only then can the world begin to dismantle the architecture of violence that masquerades as necessary foreign policy.

subject: Olivia’s DACA status lapsed, nowshe’s on unpaid leave
body:
DACA renewal delays are part of a broader pattern of erosion. | | | Peter, Some DACA recipients are losing their jobs as renewal applications now take five times longer to process than last year, causing many to lose their work authorization and current employment.1 **Olivia** came to the U.S. at three, has had DACA since 2012, and is a single mother and fourth‐grade teacher who applied for renewal in November 2025. Her work permit expired while she waited, so this Teachers Appreciation Week, she’s on unpaid leave and her students — including those with special needs — have gone without her for weeks as her family struggles to pay bills with no income. As prices soar nationwide — crushing working families — DACA renewal delays are leaving recipients exposed to the rising threat of detention and deportation, and without the financial stability to pay for rent, groceries, medical bills, and more if their DACA renewals don’t arrive on time. This is especially crushing for working and mixed-status families, who are left unsure if they’ll be able to return to their previous job or find new roles in an already challenging job market. This isn’t just a few stories — it’s widespread. **Renewal wait times have stretched past six months for many, the longest processing times in a decade.** Application delays are not just bureaucratic backlogs — they’re part of a broader pattern of erosion that is undermining DACA from every angle. As recipients wait months without clarity, they’re left exposed to losing work authorization, stability, and protection. Because here is the reality: **These delays are part of a cascading crisis weakening the DACA program piece by piece.** The threats to DACA are stacking up — one by one — weakening the entire program. We won’t sit back as DACA recipients are targeted and put at risk. The moment demands our collective action and community advocacy. Whether you’re an immigrant or a citizen, if you’re a working person in this country, **it is up to us to fight with and for each other.** **[We’ll continue working to protect DACA recipients and all immigrant youth who are being placed at risk by these policies, Peter. clean_body: DACA renewal delays are part of a broader pattern of erosion. | | | Peter, Some DACA recipients are losing their jobs as renewal applications now take five times longer to process than last year, causing many to lose their work authorization and current employment.1 Olivia came to the U.S. at three, has had DACA since 2012, and is a single mother and fourth‐grade teacher who applied for renewal in November 2025. Her work permit expired while she waited, so this Teachers Appreciation Week, she’s on unpaid leave and her students — including those with special needs — have gone without her for weeks as her family struggles to pay bills with no income. As prices soar nationwide — crushing working families — DACA renewal delays are leaving recipients exposed to the rising threat of detention and deportation, and without the financial stability to pay for rent, groceries, medical bills, and more if their DACA renewals don’t arrive on time. This is especially crushing for working and mixed-status families, who are left unsure if they’ll be able to return to their previous job or find new roles in an already challenging job market. This isn’t just a few stories — it’s widespread. Renewal wait times have stretched past six months for many, the longest processing times in a decade. Application delays are not just bureaucratic backlogs — they’re part of a broader pattern of erosion that is undermining DACA from every angle. As recipients wait months without clarity, they’re left exposed to losing work authorization, stability, and protection. Because here is the reality: These delays are part of a cascading crisis weakening the DACA program piece by piece. The threats to DACA are stacking up — one by one — weakening the entire program. We won’t sit back as DACA recipients are targeted and put at risk. The moment demands our collective action and community advocacy. Whether you’re an immigrant or a citizen, if you’re a working person in this country, it is up to us to fight with and for each other. | | _**_MEET NANCY_**_ Nancy’s Alaska story began at 18, when a two-week summer trip turned into a lifetime commitment. After working on the pipeline that first summer, she fell in love with Alaska’s rugged independence and community spirit. She and her husband, Kit, built their life here — raising four children, running a small business, and now enjoying eleven grandchildren. Through Kit’s experience as a small business owner, Nancy saw firsthand the challenges entrepreneurs face in Alaska.

Being raised in a military family taught Nancy the importance of service and always keeping your word. Her drive to solve problems and improve life for Alaska families led Nancy into public service. She served nine years in the State Legislature, where she chaired key committees on Military & Veterans Affairs and Armed Services. As a legislator, Nancy kept her promises — protecting the Permanent Fund, defending Alaska’s role in national defense, standing up to special interests, and never compromising her principles. When rising crime threatened Alaska communities under Senate Bill 91, Nancy stepped up again, serving as Commissioner of Corrections. She prioritized victims, backed law enforcement, kept dangerous criminals behind bars, and sought compassionate solutions to the addiction crisis.
Today, as Lieutenant Governor, Nancy has fought for election integrity, helped lead Alaska through challenges, and worked alongside Governor Mike Dunleavy to unleash Alaska’s energy potential and protect our way of life. With a record of balancing budgets, cutting waste, and delivering results, Nancy has the executive experience to lead.
**As Governor, Nancy will focus on:**
* **Protecting the PFD:** Defending the Permanent Fund Dividend for families today and future generations.
* **Jobs & the Economy: **Strengthening Alaska’s workforce and creating opportunity statewide
* **Energy & Cost of Living:** Supporting responsible resource development, lowering utility costs, and fighting for energy independence.
* **Public Safety:** Backing the blue, standing with victims, and keeping dangerous criminals off our streets.
* **Fiscal Responsibility:** Balancing budgets, cutting waste, and protecting taxpayers.
* **Strong Schools:** Empowering parents, focusing on literacy, and preparing students for tomorrow’s jobs.

Alaska is where Nancy found adventure, built a family, and discovered her calling to serve. She’s running for Governor to ensure Alaska remains the best place to live, work, and raise a family — for her children, her grandchildren, and for every Alaskan.

Derek, Paige here — I wanted to write a quick note to you about why I ran for mayor of Scranton. It’s an important part of my story, and key to understanding how this race will decide the future of NEPA. I ran for mayor because I couldn’t raise my family in a place where government corruption is okay. **Corruption was not a theory here; the last Mayor was indicted for extortion.** Enough was enough. That’s why I ran as an independent and launched the campaign that became known as Paige Against the Machine. I left labels at the door because this was never about party politics. It was about cleaning up a system that rewarded cronies, hid waste, and put private gain ahead of the public good. **I ran to make government work for our kids, our families, and our small businesses, not for insiders.** Running against the local machine was hard. | | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Katie’s never backed down from a fight—especially when it comes to holding MAGA extremism accountable.
In Congress, she stood up to Trump and his cronies, delivering real results for Californians. Now, she’s running for governor to keep doing exactly that.
**Because this race couldn’t be clearer: It’s MAGA’s agenda vs. California values.**
First, _Trump_ slashed nearly $30 billion from Medi-Cal, gutting care for low-income and rural communities across the state. _Katie_ is fighting for a single-payer health care system focused on delivering high-quality, affordable care for _everyone._
Then, _Trump_ claimed we can’t afford child care while prioritizing funding for his illegal war overseas. _Katie_ is pushing for universal child care—because she knows families shouldn’t choose between work and raising their kids.
Now, _Trump’s_ endorsed Steve Hilton, a candidate prepared to bring his extremist agenda to California. _Katie_ , on the other hand, is running to deliver real change and protect Californians from Trump’s attacks.
Corporate donors are pouring millions into this race to protect the status quo and give MAGA allies a real shot at power.
Katie is the _only_ candidate in this race who’s refused corporate PAC money. She’s relying on grassroots supporters to step up and help us fight back against MAGA’s agenda—** _and win._**

Peter,
---
It's Gary Sinise here. You may know me from my roles in movies like Apollo 13 _ _ and The Green Mile or the CBS television series CSI: NY - but it was in 1994 playing the role of Lt. Dan in Forrest Gump that changed my life and inspired my enduring connection to our defenders, veterans, and first responders. I've served as an Honorary Grand Marshal for the National Memorial Day Parade in Washington, D.C. nearly every year since American Veterans Center revived it in 2005. **But I've never been more excited to serve as an Honorary Grand Marshall than I am this year - the year of America's 250****th**** birthday.**

Peter, this Memorial Day marks the first major national act of remembrance of the veterans who made the ultimate sacrifice to defend America from its enemies and ensure it has remained the Land of the Free for the last 250 years. And this year's National Memorial Day Parade will be a special edition - the biggest parade yet - where national memory meets living history as veterans from every military generation celebrate America and honor the service and sacrifice of their fallen brethren. **Peter, the National Memorial Day Parade is ENIRELY FUNDED by private contributions, including from generous patriots like you.** **[In light of America’s 250th birthday and the special opportunity we have to honor veterans this year, will you chip in today to help support the parade with a gift of $25, $50, $75, $150, or more?](http://links.freedomtrainalert.com/u/click?_t=2d4f229f156142619b4e4f956d2d65c9&_m=d77cd611f8084edcac0c2a864bebf48f&_e=aAlf6JvZHdyP5heIPF7EVsceUQK4v6dH3-kPnw_6i3pwdljXIeH0jnzdKnPzpp022gzTPoo9DXSvOpwDMwSdDnInHXNTPSSAgCy7up-etZQXSEhstUTB9FCO4bWxrT_dDTjOzIhrpepugxtixpC4Ew2fOE_Z9asZdTIPtCQKyi9iKMi1xEf2eBMvO0V7MCKUldD5YCPcw9wce2DjedOaZIUVi_ny-QFIJJmXJ0uQpqAzfztldAAy0KXfrckjQIJwSELj0RVivOfCw5cWTDxySEtftO3a8PQP-u8kb2YXS-35Jy3jztwHfZqVAocTMEx-H2ttdrNA9kMBArQfHW1tGDcAG3AJFAuvvW5ypF_m8FsnvYLKwwTbtt7HULg5n0pMNDHZgIj4NzHKK-RkQYTdanytZPZybfEZnJ3lkvBpo7qvIfwTNfQTqir9Bp4OP6TXFAklyIRdrLyDLZcd2ShCLqWWtuw5cZwPj1euEM78-Xn-YtOzctwQ5OdCJPwEpGq42Mwcv8MOUfBbAbQPIupI9FJpQBzZ794ofHTOkj7mIHojAd8fOCTCOehzofQNesecQGzfICNAzhDm_-jjukdtBfozVE1EAblB6q-nHjG1Ze1KPVTD0L9uVPhJM-yY-Ia-BcoJIrG7LpGZa5XBb2Z_fngns0ePuCjw9orYpXpMFbVsYlUrzrbg6dT0priloqiujLOVOuE7W4ZcYM90x_nEGg%3D%3D)**

On Memorial Day - not just this momentous year of military milestones, but every year - please join me in honoring those who made the ultimate sacrifice for our freedoms. Come to the National Memorial Day Parade in Washington, D.C. Visit a local veterans' cemetery. Send a note to a family of the fallen. Or simply take a quiet moment to think about the men and women who gave their lives to defend OUR country. I believe that while we can never do enough to express our gratitude to our defenders, veterans, and first responders, we can always do a little more. **Peter, thank you for your support of America 's heroes. ** [**And please, if you’re able, make a gift to fund the National Memorial Day parade right now during America’s 250****th****birthday.**](http://links.freedomtrainalert.com/u/click?_t=2d4f229f156142619b4e4f956d2d65c9&_m=d77cd611f8084edcac0c2a864bebf48f&_e=aAlf6JvZHdyP5heIPF7EVsceUQK4v6dH3-kPnw_6i3pwdljXIeH0jnzdKnPzpp022gzTPoo9DXSvOpwDMwSdDnInHXNTPSSAgCy7up-etZQXSEhstUTB9FCO4bWxrT_dDTjOzIhrpepugxtixpC4Ew2fOE_Z9asZdTIPtCQKyi9iKMi1xEf2eBMvO0V7MCKUldD5YCPcw9wce2DjedOaZIUVi_ny-QFIJJmXJ0uQpqAzfztldAAy0KXfrckjQIJwE-5xNpQDyw-Pjo-LxOFsrStA3GygAwHxzpvAM1mgWlcVsIUybUvZiMGGb-vuF9Zgz-pEfMUAKMsT7whg3G7nvlRx6sC-6_egAZyFCdfwmxNxMRDQ7822XIDvM5yU9jCQJI1XV2l-5eN5uDQN5eMSdJJvPBNWfA-R3Ig5R7qicmZr4LO27D2kvC3Abm2aO81F0UIovbzrNxII5fbUMVDpPqgBPwf6fFq63LxFkq7ZECuHmEmw50iujWnGZdPiRD_NY39GjOZL8BUSFydJpQ0QfrSfrRlO-_DmXH96stI4BGULP8b79XgOeskSrpzaRna9_aw4DH32IMiaHsXWzqlHc-P-7VkUajjKNfNcSgw5gdwZfBUtMUdMQotjQusrbRD6yZiqNdmJTTUJ84ctNxyy8rxwZyoKL2EFLjh1z9mEWxqQTVKp1udPznsRuBVCztYoIA7l0L7eke_sxhNQlsNgrw%3D%3D)

clean_body: As America turns 250, we must honor them while we can | | | | Peter, It's Gary Sinise here. You may know me from my roles in movies like Apollo 13 and The Green Mile or the CBS television series CSI: NY - but it was in 1994 playing the role of Lt. Dan in Forrest Gump that changed my life and inspired my enduring connection to our defenders, veterans, and first responders. I've served as an Honorary Grand Marshal for the National Memorial Day Parade in Washington, D.C. nearly every year since American Veterans Center revived it in 2005. But I've never been more excited to serve as an Honorary Grand Marshall than I am this year - the year of America's 250th birthday. Peter, this Memorial Day marks the first major national act of remembrance of the veterans who made the ultimate sacrifice to defend America from its enemies and ensure it has remained the Land of the Free for the last 250 years. And this year's National Memorial Day Parade will be a special edition - the biggest parade yet - where national memory meets living history as veterans from every military generation celebrate America and honor the service and sacrifice of their fallen brethren. Peter, the National Memorial Day Parade is ENIRELY FUNDED by private contributions, including from generous patriots like you. WWII veterans were a key part of the first parade when it was revived in 2005, as they have been every year since for the last 20 years. But this may be the last year we have the opportunity to have these brave men and women with us for the parade. | | | | | | | | This year is a rare moment when living witnesses to World War II and America 's 250th birthday overlap. And no matter how much you can give to this important cause, I want to ask something additional of you. On Memorial Day - not just this momentous year of military milestones, but every year - please join me in honoring those who made the ultimate sacrifice for our freedoms. Come to the National Memorial Day Parade in Washington, D.C. Visit a local veterans' cemetery. Send a note to a family of the fallen. Or simply take a quiet moment to think about the men and women who gave their lives to defend OUR country. I believe that while we can never do enough to express our gratitude to our defenders, veterans, and first responders, we can always do a little more. Peter, thank you for your support of America 's heroes. Sincerely, Tim Holbert President American Veterans Center | | | The mission of the American Veterans Center and the World War II Veterans Committee is to preserve and promote the legacy and experiences of America's veterans and active duty service personnel from World War II through today. Together, the four of us represent something you need to understand: we are the only four Black men ever elected to the U.S. House of Representatives from Louisiana since 1877.
| | | | | [](https://6oz8v8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001AYAwHdR29uldBayve5iRyhm7IKtcrU7iKEMaOjRbWzIv0TDK4xvfBNcBA-1IpF9IsDABoNZtujkPhnuRtEVyvlrwb81RulHEw8ta2Aodv0hUKnYE5t0WgDDQyeIII638eWhIr2VXFii9y6iCrOXr4m5INYjDr2nm4I6_DQ6jfL-4AlKp9cMQep5NtbhI95ezh6x0xmiLFm1q7Ep76DWX-WneRFiMWUED&c=-Coy6JjbTAuNpIGXGL9yYsC6IsdA4hAFjQ99rVceh2L-1Rio5qxHww==&ch=TxJ4CpHmhSQ_TP1hF6cXWukxJLSjdAxliTDGQ2684YurYmF0joVX2A==)

| | | |
Peter,
Today, I testified in front of the Louisiana state legislature against MAGA's plan to erase my district and to take Louisiana back to the era of Jim Crow. I was not alone. Joining me were former Congressmen William J. Jefferson and Cedric Richmond, and current Congressman Troy Carter.
Together, the four of us represent something you need to understand: we are the only four Black men ever elected to the U.S. House of Representatives from Louisiana since 1877.
---
| | [](https://6oz8v8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001AYAwHdR29uldBayve5iRyhm7IKtcrU7iKEMaOjRbWzIv0TDK4xvfBNcBA-1IpF9IsDABoNZtujkPhnuRtEVyvlrwb81RulHEw8ta2Aodv0hUKnYE5t0WgDDQyeIII638eWhIr2VXFii9y6iCrOXr4m5INYjDr2nm4I6_DQ6jfL-4AlKp9cMQep5NtbhI95ezh6x0xmiLFm0AyltKTzLrLqMW_M5qD4Hq&c=-Coy6JjbTAuNpIGXGL9yYsC6IsdA4hAFjQ99rVceh2L-1Rio5qxHww==&ch=TxJ4CpHmhSQ_TP1hF6cXWukxJLSjdAxliTDGQ2684YurYmF0joVX2A==)
---
Four. In nearly 150 years. In a state where Black people make up more than a third of the population. That is the legacy of Jim Crow. That is what racist, discriminatory congressional maps look like -- maps drawn specifically to silence Black voters and make sure we never had a voice in our own government.
Last week, a Supreme Court packed with unelected right-wing extremists gutted the Voting Rights Act -- the landmark legislation that Civil Rights leaders fought to secure. The very next day, Governor Jeff Landry suspended the ongoing May 16th congressional elections under a manufactured "state of emergency" so that he could shove a gerrymandered map through the legislature and eliminate Louisiana's only majority-Black congressional districts.
[That's why I was at the Capitol today. I am fighting a battle of a lifetime to prevent the return of Jim Crow in Louisiana. Fighting to prevent Black Louisianans from losing their voice in Congress entirely. And I need the help from Democrats everywhere in this fight for justice.](https://6oz8v8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001AYAwHdR29uldBayve5iRyhm7IKtcrU7iKEMaOjRbWzIv0TDK4xvfBNcBA-1IpF9IsDABoNZtujkPhnuRtEVyvlrwb81RulHEw8ta2Aodv0hUKnYE5t0WgDDQyeIII638eWhIr2VXFii9y6iCrOXr4m5INYjDr2nm4I6_DQ6jfL-4AlKp9cMQep5NtbhI95ezh6x0xmiLFm0Fgj_K91sZJkfxpgpdPuOH&c=-Coy6JjbTAuNpIGXGL9yYsC6IsdA4hAFjQ99rVceh2L-1Rio5qxHww==&ch=TxJ4CpHmhSQ_TP1hF6cXWukxJLSjdAxliTDGQ2684YurYmF0joVX2A==)
I have joined a historic lawsuit against our MAGA governor to stop this unprecedented theft of an election. And if they succeed in shoving me into a redder district, I am rapidly scaling my campaign to compete and win against all odds.
As a Black Democrat from the Deep South, I know how to win tough battles. But I will not lie to you. I am now in the fight of my life. I need a massive surge of small dollar donations to withstand the onslaught I now face.
[Please Peter, can I count on you to rush a donation of $50, $25, or whatever is meaningful to you to help me fight against the return of Jim Crow in Louisiana?](https://6oz8v8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001AYAwHdR29uldBayve5iRyhm7IKtcrU7iKEMaOjRbWzIv0TDK4xvfBNcBA-1IpF9IqppnSwB2Loa-vS1rKLpq1H58sA9cuLcL8-hNtO1DsBZi63IV44V0Fs2PxoIpwFKTu6u-SGeB4Y3CIJzWrvwKh5AMEoZvEHMjuxLX-oSeEe2CYU83V4yKZFNwgqeFFLIZn6BzdquKXuo__2Ku6nNnHAJNu6jPXQfvLH4WxQE7IQg=&c=-Coy6JjbTAuNpIGXGL9yYsC6IsdA4hAFjQ99rVceh2L-1Rio5qxHww==&ch=TxJ4CpHmhSQ_TP1hF6cXWukxJLSjdAxliTDGQ2684YurYmF0joVX2A==)

**She Flatlined ... and Found Peace: The Story Behind The long awaited new book- "**_**Story to Stage "**_
She survived a serial killer. Then her own body tried to finish the job.
One ordinary Tuesday, **Ginine Emily Smith** walked up a flight of stairs... and collapsed.
In the ambulance, her heart stopped. Every number in her bloodwork hit zero.
And in that space, between life and death, she experienced something she had never felt before.
**Peace.**
The kind of peace that doesn't come from performance.The kind of peace that doesn't come from doing more, achieving more, or being more.The kind of peace that can only come from truth.
And when she woke up -everything had to change.
**The Hidden Struggle No One Talks About**
From the outside, Ginine had built a life most people would admire. She was a high-performing leader, a successful stage performer, a creative force, and a woman who consistently showed up, pushed through, and carried it all with strength.
But on the inside, she was depleted. Like so many women, she had quietly learned how to survive rather than truly live. She coped through constant work and relentless busyness, through wine and food, through the pressure of always being the "strong one" for everyone else. She even hid within the rhythms of church life.
Because sometimes, the greatest hiding place is a life that appears to be working.
And that's the tension at the heart of her new book:
[Story to Stage: The Badass Guide to Rising from Pain to Power:](https://substack.com/redirect/76bcbf97-cbc4-4180-95cf-bac1fd878b70?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
This is not just a memoir, nor is it just another self-help book filled with inspiration and no direction. **It 's a wake-up call.**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4c78539e-c824-46a4-bf3b-2dfc6774435d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**A Story You Couldn 't Make Up If You Tried**
In _Story to Stage_ , Ginine pulls back the curtain on a life shaped by extremes.
Growing up in a home where addiction and depression lived in every room.
Losing her father at fifteen.
Navigating years of survival, searching, and reinvention.
And at twenty-one--unknowingly befriending the East Side serial killer, George Russell.
Yes. That kind of story.
But here's what makes this book different:
She doesn't tell her story for shock value.
She tells it to show you what's possible on the other side of it because the real story isn't what happened to her. **It 's what she chose to do with it.**
**From Pain ... to Platform**
What Ginine discovered--and now teaches globally--is this:
**Your story doesn 't disqualify you. It positions you.**
But only if you learn how to own it.
That's where her signature RISE & ROAR frameworks come in.
This is the methodology behind _Story to Stage_ --the same system she uses to help women, leaders, and creatives go from **unknown to unforgettable**.
This is not through performing or pretending- But by becoming fully aligned.
**RISE -- The Internal Shift**
* **Reconnect** to your identity and voice
* **Integrate** your past instead of hiding it
* **Storytell** with truth, not trauma
* **Empower** yourself into aligned action

**ROAR -- The External Activation**
* **Reveal** your message
* **Own** your voice and presence
* **Activate** your platform and visibility
* **Rise** into influence, impact, and income

This is lived experience--refined over decades on stages, in leadership, and through real transformation.
**Why This Book Hits Different**
Most books will tell you to heal first... then act.
Ginine challenges that completely. **Healing and action happen together.**
You don't need another decade sitting in your pain, nor do you need to be "fully healed" to begin.
You need a roadmap, a witness whose life testifies to what's possible with God, and the truth that brings transformation.
Inside _Story to Stage_ , readers will discover:
* Why high-achieving can actually be a form of numbing
* How to rewrite your story before it rewrites you
* The 3 keynote secrets that turn invisible women into unforgettable speakers
* Voice and embodiment techniques that make people lean in
* How to build a platform that works--even when you're not in the room

And most importantly--**How to stop hiding.**
**For the Woman Who Knows She Was Made for More**
This book is written for the woman who appears to have it all together on the outside, yet feels deeply disconnected from her own voice, identity, and purpose. It is for the woman who has endured more than she gives herself credit for--who has survived, adapted, and carried on, but knows there is something more within her waiting to be expressed.
It is for the woman who senses a message inside her--one rooted in her experiences, her resilience, and her truth--but isn't yet sure how to articulate it, own it, or bring it into the world with confidence and clarity. It is especially for the woman standing in her next chapter, ready to rise into a new level of visibility, impact, and alignment.
Here is the truth: You are not too old. You are not too broken. You are not too late.
Your story is not something to move past or minimize. It is your assignment--your platform for influence, your pathway to purpose, and your opportunity to lead, connect, and create meaningful impact.
**The Invitation**
If you do not own your story--your story will own you.
*Other people's opinions will own you.
*Your past will own you.
But the moment you decide to rise, everything shifts.
_Story to Stage: The Baddass Guide to Rising from Pain to Power ([www.story-to-stage.com](https://substack.com/redirect/4484fb63-9e05-4e4a-a07a-45984b24c62d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_
is your invitation to:
👉 Reclaim your voice
👉 Step onto your stage
👉 And build a life and platform that reflects who you truly are
Not someday. **Now.**
Because the world doesn't need another perfect voice.
It needs a **real one.**
And yours?
It's been waiting long enough.

The stakes in our race for Georgia governor just got higher:

**FIRST:** The Supreme Court completely dismantled the Voting Rights Act, giving Republicans a green light to disenfranchise Black voters with extreme gerrymandering.

**THEN:** Trump’s handpicked gubernatorial candidate Burt Jones made it clear that if he wins this race, he’ll approve gerrymandered maps that eliminate fair representation.

I’m not asking you to choose between New Hampshire and the rest of the map. I’m telling you New Hampshire is the map.
Folks, it’s James Carville.
I’ve worked Senate races in every corner of the country, and I know how to read a map. So hear me when I say this: **New Hampshire is keeping me up at night.**
I’m watching this year’s races closely, and money is pouring into Georgia, North Carolina, Ohio, Texas, Alaska, and Maine. That’s critical because those races are part of Democrats’ path to retaking the Senate.
But here’s what’s scaring the hell out of me: **If Chris Pappas loses New Hampshire, Democrats need to flip FIVE seats instead of four to take back the Senate. That math doesn’t work. Full stop.**
**[Before you read another word, chip in $10 or whatever you can to Chris Pappas and Heartland Patriots to make sure New Hampshire doesn’t become the reason Democrats lose the Senate.](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/104422?refcode=em20260508-10463&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1&akid=10463%2E614464%2E323oQU)**

---
Chris is up just one point. One. 45-44. **That is a tied race.** And while the whole country is staring at Georgia and North Carolina, New Hampshire is sitting there in a dead heat with nobody riding to the rescue.
John Sununu — yeah, _those Sununus_ — has the name, the money, and a Republican machine that knows exactly what’s at stake here. They don’t need to flip five seats. They just need to flip New Hampshire red and let the map do the rest.
And right now? **They’ve got a real shot at doing exactly that.**
Chris Pappas is the only guy who can win this seat. He’s won the toughest district in New Hampshire four damn times. He knows how to bring people together. But he cannot — _cannot_ — do this alone when every check is being written and every eyeball is looking somewhere else.
So here’s what I need from you:
**[Rush a contribution split between Chris Pappas and Heartland Patriots today. $10, $25, $30, whatever you can spare. Because if we let this seat slip away while everybody’s watching Georgia, we’re gonna wake up in November and wonder how the hell we let it happen.](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/104422?refcode=em20260508-10463&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=9&akid=10463%2E614464%2E323oQU)**
I’m not asking you to choose between New Hampshire and the rest of the map. I’m telling you New Hampshire _is_ the map. You hold this seat, and Democrats have a real path to the majority. You lose it, and it doesn’t matter what happens in North Carolina, Texas, Maine, or anywhere else.
Don’t let New Hampshire be the reason we come up one seat short.
**[Give what you can right now.](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/104422?refcode=em20260508-10463&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=10&akid=10463%2E614464%2E323oQU)** Let’s win this damn thing and flip control of the Senate.
— James Carville

body:
Simply put: This decision will swing more seats in the short term than the controversial mid-decade redistricting efforts that ate up so much media attention over the last year. We're watching in real-time as an entire political movement chooses the pursuit of absolute power over the fundamental rights of the people.
Please, RUSH $35 or more right now to provide the resources we need to fight for everything the Voting Rights Act stood for >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=050826_2&amount=35]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
CNN: Efforts to game the 2026 election intensify as Republicans draw new maps [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=050826_2&amount=25]
The immediate impact shows how partisan the Louisiana v. Callais case before the Supreme Court was, Team.
In the week since this decision, five states have already moved to redraw their maps , dilute the impact of minority voters, and return parts of the country to a suppressive era we thought we left behind sixty years ago. Louisiana itself stopped an election with voting already in progress , and other states are moving to change their own maps soon.
CNN says this has created " an unprecedented amount of flux in American democracy six months before Election Day ." Candidates don’t know where to run. Lawmakers are seeing their districts carved up. Voters don’t know which district they live in.
This is all about power. Whether districts are fair or everyone is represented has been tossed by the wayside for MAGA's desperate grasp to control a country that's more disillusioned with their actions by the day.
Team: We can't change this SCOTUS decision but we can help elect pro-democracy candidates up and down the ballot. Step up with $35 or whatever you can today and help us defend the right to vote >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=050826_2&amount=35]

Striking down the last remnants of the Voting Rights Act is exactly why the Supreme Court held this case over from last year. Gutting Section 2, which requires that racial minorities have an equal opportunity to meaningfully participate in the electoral process , is going to take us backwards in time and allow racial gerrymandering to be a standard practice, silencing more voters.
Long before the MAGA movement, Chief Justice Roberts saw the removal of the VRA as one of his top goals for his time on the Court. President Trump followed this decision with a directive for conservative-led states to erase multiple majority-Black districts across the South. His supporters are climbing over one another to comply.
The consequences are simple to understand and grave for voter participation. The harder we make it to vote, the more politicians make voter participation feel worthless, the less people actually take part. Needless to say, the less people who participate, the less our democracy and our government looks like the people it's supposed to represent.
The answer is to beat them at the ballot box and elect candidates who support our fundamental right to vote. Will you chip in with $35 or whatever you can to help us fight back against their desperate ploy to hold power? >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=050826_2&amount=35]

Integrity First Voter Action Project is dedicated to expanding ballot access and increasing voter participation across the country.
Since the Supreme Court gutted key provisions in the Voting Rights Act, extreme politicians have taken advantage to pass harsh laws that restrict access to the ballot box. These restrictions particularly affect disadvantaged communities and people of color. It’s our goal to bring awareness to these laws wherever they may crop up and organize voters to take action to ensure the right to vote is available to everyone in their states and communities.

Peter,

Right now, families across Washington and across the country are getting squeezed at the gas pump.

Since the start of President Trump's reckless war in Iran, nationwide gas prices have jumped by **more than a dollar per gallon.** Here in Washington state, **we've crossed $5.75, and in the Seattle area, we're seeing the highest prices on record.**

There’s no sugarcoating it: Donald Trump just fired all 22 members of the National Science Board.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jc_dsg-em?refcode=260508EM-fires-rs [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jc_dsg-em?refcode=260508EM-fires-rs]
FIGHT BACK [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jc_dsg-em?refcode=260508EM-fires-rs]
This is the governing body overseeing the National Science Foundation, one of the most important scientific institutions in the United States — and he fired all of them. At once.
The National Science Board exists for a reason. It oversees billions in federal research funding, advises Congress on science policy, and helps ensure taxpayer dollars support real, evidence-based innovation.
Now that independence is being stripped away.
Let me say this clearly: When political leaders start dismantling independent science institutions, it doesn’t just hurt scientists. It hurts all of us — because that means fewer medical breakthroughs, less climate research, slower progress on cancer treatments, degraded pandemic preparedness, and more.
As a microbiologist and educator, take it from me: Science only works when it is allowed to be independent, transparent, and guided by evidence — not politics.
But what we’re seeing now is a systematic effort to replace expertise with loyalty, and it’s happening at the highest levels of government.
This is exactly why I’m running for Congress. Because we need leaders who will defend science and protect vital institutions like the NSF.
But I can’t take on that fight alone. We’re heading into a critical stretch of this campaign, and we need the resources to compete against entrenched interests that are perfectly comfortable ignoring science. So I’m asking you: Can you chip in $10 or whatever you can today to help me fight for science, facts, and the future of research in America? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jc_dsg-em?refcode=260508EM-fires-rs]
DONATE NOW [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jc_dsg-em?refcode=260508EM-fires-rs]
When we let science lead, people thrive. Let’s put facts back in charge — and build a Congress that reflects reason, reality, and hope.
Thank you,
Dr. Jasmine Clark

A shocking new poll just dropped showing Deep State conspirator Alexander Vindman within just three points of flipping Florida in our must-win Senate special election.

Three points. That's within the margin of error. In other words, this race is effectively tied. Let that sink in.

The man who abused his position at the highest levels of our government, who drove the Trump impeachment from inside the National Security Council, who wasted millions of taxpayer dollars trying to bring down a duly elected president -- that man is now knocking on the door of the United States Senate. In Florida. In President Trump's home state.

Vindman has made no secret of what drives him. He's not running out of some deep love of Florida -- he just moved here! This is a man vehemently opposed to everything we stand for, singularly obsessed with destroying the America First Agenda, and determined to make every Trump supporter pay the price.

This is not ambition. This is cold, hard revenge - and now he has the money to make it real.

Vindman has raised over $8 million -- radical left-wing cash pouring in from the most extreme Trump-hating mega-donors in the country. Every dollar is fuel for his revenge campaign.

And here's what makes this even more alarming: Democrats don't just have a candidate -- they have momentum. In the last month alone, Democrats flipped three Florida seats. If Vindman flips this seat, Democrats take back the Senate majority -- and nothing stands between them and another impeachment, endless obstruction, and a complete dismantling of everything we've built.

President Trump is fixing up Washington, D.C., the way he fixes up everything else: like a builder who actually notices when something looks like hell. He's spent the last year and a half quietly turning the nation's capital from a tired, graffiti-scarred mess into something that doesn't make people want to look away. He's cleaning monuments, making the fountains work again, restoring reflecting pools, and slapping classical architecture back on federal buildings that had spent decades dressed like concrete bunkers and he's doing it without apology.
The latest flare-up came on May 8, 2026, when ABC reporter Rachel Scott asked Trump **[why he was bothering with"beautification projects" in the middle of international tension.](https://substack.com/redirect/6463aa85-2d56-4e5c-b761-4a7374c96ef3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** Trump didn't hesitate. **" Because I want to keep our country beautiful and safe,"** he shot back.

This isn't some side hobby. Trump has always seen himself as a builder, and Washington suits him. He's spent decades putting up towers and golf courses that people actually want to visit. Now he's applying the same eye to the national capital. From the White House ballroom to the reflecting pool, the message is the same: bring the splendor back. The city had been sliding into neglect--filthy walkways, crumbling stonework, buildings that looked more like parking garages than symbols of anything important. Trump's crews have been pressure-washing, replanting, and repairing. The results are visible. Tourists aren't dodging litter. Federal grounds look cared for again. Regular people notice that kind of thing.

The policy backbone came in an Executive Order, signed in August 2025 under the title **["Making Federal Architecture Beautiful Again."](https://substack.com/redirect/69a3fd59-f156-4c4e-8f79-19994186ec68?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** It's blunt about what went wrong. For roughly 150 years after the founding, federal buildings followed classical lines--think the Capitol and the White House, modeled on ancient Athens and Rome to remind citizens what self-government is supposed to look like. Then the 1960s hit, and the government switched to modernist and brutalist designs that most Americans hated on sight. The order calls those out for what they were: unpopular, uninspiring, and often just plain ugly. It directs the General Services Administration to default to classical and traditional architecture in D.C., especially for courthouses, agency headquarters, and any big-ticket federal project over $50 million. No more boxy concrete eyesores **unless there 's a damn good reason.**

But this is _SO MUCH_ bigger than just one election... **[THIS](https://substack.com/redirect/21485ba9-25ee-4b9e-a2e7-fce2ae6ced7b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** will set the liberal agenda back _**DECADES**_.

The order doesn't stop at new construction. It pushes for restoring existing monuments and increasing architectural grandeur wherever possible. It's workmanlike government--do the job right, use proven designs, spend money where it shows.

Friend, When I look at what I have been able to accomplish in life, even this race for governor, I can’t help but see the dedicated teachers that helped shape and support me on this path. This _Teacher Appreciation Week,_ let’s take a moment to recognize something simple but powerful:_**great schools start with great teachers.**_

Across our state, **teachers show up every day for their students** , often with shamefully limited resources, growing class sizes, and far too little support, let alone thanks. They do it anyway. Day after day, they stay late and they show up early. They care deeply, often using their own money to buy school supplies, or clothing, or food for students in need. They face shifting demands and metrics from lawmakers, as they nevertheless shape our shared future in ways that can’t be measured by test scores alone. **Jerri Green believes it’s time our policies reflect that reality, and show some respect for these dedicated public servants.** **Her plan is clear:**
* _**Fully fund public schools**_ so teachers have the resources they need
* _**Raise teacher pay**_ and restore respect to the profession
* _**Invest in support staff**_ like counselors and nurses so teachers aren’t stretched beyond their roles
* _**Expand special education resources**_ and recruit more educators into these critical positions
* _**Provide students with stronger mental health and learning support,**_ creating better classroom environments for everyone

**This isn’t just about performative appreciation through platitudes, it’s about putting policy and funding behind our promises.** If we truly value teachers, we need to back that up with real investment and real change. _That’s exactly what this campaign is fighting for._ **As we celebrate Teacher Appreciation Week, we’re asking you to stand with educators across our state.** Help us build a future where every teacher is supported, every classroom is fully funded, and every student has the opportunity to succeed. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/131034303/619708664/2105508926?refcode=ea.d7eba753-0f4b-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&ms=ea.d7eba753-0f4b-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImQ3ZWJhNzUzLTBmNGItZjExMS04ZWYyLTAwMGQzYTE0YjY0MCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=wYEti_ywSwK_1MaGcEkaXeYmWElOJn7uTwTl5jSa4CE=) Friend — in 2022, I was diagnosed with non-Hodgkin's lymphoma. I went through months of chemotherapy. Countless medical visits. Some very hard days. I was lucky to have access to incredible doctors and effective treatments that saved my life. But not everyone is so lucky. That painful truth has stayed with me, and it's the reason I am writing to you today about a landmark Supreme Court case that hits close to home. The case is about Roundup, the weedkiller made by pharmaceutical and biotech giant Bayer. For years, people who developed non-Hodgkin's lymphoma after using Roundup have sued the company, alleging the herbicide caused their cancer and that Bayer failed to warn them about the risks. Now Bayer is asking the Supreme Court to wipe away a 2023 verdict won by a Missouri gardener who developed non-Hodgkin’s lymphoma after using Roundup and was awarded $1.25 million in damages. **If Bayer wins at the Supreme Court, more than 11,500 people with similar cases could be jeopardized.** This corporate giant wants the Court to make sure no one, in any state, could ever hold it accountable for failing to warn about potential cancer risks. And to make matters worse, earlier this year, the Trump administration invoked wartime-era powers to protect the production of glyphosate-based herbicides, the very products at the center of the Roundup cancer lawsuits. _Think about what this means._ Tens of thousands of people who say they got cancer after using a product sold without adequate warning labels could be told by the highest court in the country that they have no right to hold the corporation behind it accountable. **Surviving cancer changed me. It made me think deeply about the time I have left — and how I want to use it. I do not want to look back with regret. I want to know I did everything I could to fight for a future where corporations cannot put people’s health at risk and then walk away from the consequences.** That's why our work at JanePAC has never felt more urgent and personal to me. Electing climate champions — at every level of government — is how we protect our communities from this kind of harm. It's how we make sure the people writing our laws and enforcing our standards actually believe that human health matters more than corporate profits. A ruling from the Supreme Court is expected by the end of June or early July. We'll be watching closely, and I'll be back in touch when we know more. | [DONATE](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/131034304/619708666/2105508926?refcode=ea.d7eba753-0f4b-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&ms=ea.d7eba753-0f4b-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk2NzgyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImQ3ZWJhNzUzLTBmNGItZjExMS04ZWYyLTAwMGQzYTE0YjY0MCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=wYEti_ywSwK_1MaGcEkaXeYmWElOJn7uTwTl5jSa4CE=)

Jane Fonda

clean_body: | = Friend — in 2022, I was diagnosed with non-Hodgkin's lymphoma. I went through months of chemotherapy. Countless medical visits. Some very hard days. I was lucky to have access to incredible doctors and effective treatments that saved my life. But not everyone is so lucky. That painful truth has stayed with me, and it's the reason I am writing to you today about a landmark Supreme Court case that hits close to home. The case is about Roundup, the weedkiller made by pharmaceutical and biotech giant Bayer. For years, people who developed non-Hodgkin's lymphoma after using Roundup have sued the company, alleging the herbicide caused their cancer and that Bayer failed to warn them about the risks. Now Bayer is asking the Supreme Court to wipe away a 2023 verdict won by a Missouri gardener who developed non-Hodgkin’s lymphoma after using Roundup and was awarded $1.25 million in damages. If Bayer wins at the Supreme Court, more than 11,500 people with similar cases could be jeopardized. This corporate giant wants the Court to make sure no one, in any state, could ever hold it accountable for failing to warn about potential cancer risks. And to make matters worse, earlier this year, the Trump administration invoked wartime-era powers to protect the production of glyphosate-based herbicides, the very products at the center of the Roundup cancer lawsuits. Think about what this means. Tens of thousands of people who say they got cancer after using a product sold without adequate warning labels could be told by the highest court in the country that they have no right to hold the corporation behind it accountable. Surviving cancer changed me. It made me think deeply about the time I have left — and how I want to use it. I do not want to look back with regret. I want to know I did everything I could to fight for a future where corporations cannot put people’s health at risk and then walk away from the consequences. That's why our work at JanePAC has never felt more urgent and personal to me. Electing climate champions — at every level of government — is how we protect our communities from this kind of harm. It's how we make sure the people writing our laws and enforcing our standards actually believe that human health matters more than corporate profits. A ruling from the Supreme Court is expected by the end of June or early July. We'll be watching closely, and I'll be back in touch when we know more. | = In solidarity, Jane Fonda | = | = = Follow along: | | | | | ---|---|---|---|---|--- Paid for by Jane Fonda Climate PAC, not authorized by any candidate or candidate’s committee. Peter,

Eric Swalwell and Tony Gonzalez may have been pressured into giving up their seats in Congress, but they are still eligible to receive taxpayer-funded retirement benefits.

That’s unacceptable.

Representatives Subramanyam, Walkshaw, and I have been working across the aisle with Congresswomen Boebert, Mace, and Luna to prohibit any Congressperson found guilty of sex crimes, crimes of violence, or of engaging in sexual relationships with their staff from receiving a taxpayer funded pension.

I am proud to stand with survivors in the face of a Congress that has – for far too long – protected violent and vile men.

The time for accountability is long overdue. No more taxpayer money should be going into the pockets of sick and twisted people. That’s what the Congressional Pension Integrity Act would solve for.

There’s no excuse for members of Congress using their status and power to engage in sexually or otherwise violent behavior or relationships. Full stop.

Americans are sick of being let down by the people elected to represent them. We already strip taxpayer-funded pensions from Members convicted of corruption, bribery, and treason – sexual assault and harassment must be taken just as seriously.

That’s what you sent me here to do: to fight corruption and abuse of power. That's exactly what I’m going to do.

Every single time.

– Emily Randall

subject: The Mountain Minute: 5/8/2026
body:
Big business taxes, small family credits, and a permanent tax on overtime
| | | | [](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
---
**PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
| | Hi friends!
Want your full news breakdown? Listen to the Mountain Minute podcast [here](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), or watch on [YouTube](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) or [Rumble](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). Here's a summary of today's top stories:
**🏛️ Under the Golden Dome...** With _five days left_ in session, lawmakers are battling over spending, crime, energy, and government power. A Senate panel [rejected expanded lawsuits against state officials](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). Lawmakers also advanced a tax package raising business taxes and [permanently taxing federally exempt overtime pay](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). Budget tensions continue over a $1.5 billion shortfall and [planned legislator pay raises](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), while lawmakers push to [extend operations at a coal plant](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) over reliability concerns.
**🏔️ Here in Colorado...** [Gas prices nearing $4.50 a gallon](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) are squeezing drivers, truckers, and working families. Energy policy is also taking center stage in Colorado’s congressional races as scrutiny grows around proposals that could [tighten regulations on the state’s only oil refinery](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). Meanwhile, Colorado is facing its lowest snowpack in more than four decades, [worsening drought concerns](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) statewide, while a former EEOC official & congressional candidate is hosting free Colorado workshops on workplace discrimination rights as Congress faces [renewed harassment scrutiny](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.).
**🇺🇸 On the National Stage/Commentary Spotlight...** The Trump administration is reshaping healthcare and gun policy as HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. pushes to [reduce antidepressant overprescribing](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)—especially for children—while the DOJ and ATF [roll back several Biden-era firearm regulations](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) following President Trump’s executive order on Second Amendment protections. Commentary surrounding the [National Day of Prayer](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) also highlighted renewed focus on faith, personal responsibility, and national unity.
This is your Mountain Minute for Friday, May 8, 2026.
– Team RMV
---
|
---
**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[Manny Rutinel wants to represent Colorado’s oil country. His law is bearing down on its only refinery.](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY JEN SCHUMANN, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
State Rep. Manny Rutinel is asking voters in the heart of Colorado’s oil country to send him to Congress. Seven weeks from now, a law Rutinel helped write could reshape how Colorado’s only petroleum refinery operates.
The Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment published a refinery assessment on May 1 after HB24-1338—the 2024 bill Rutinel co-sponsored—required the state to conduct it.
The state hired Eastern Research Group to do the work. ERG compared Suncor’s Commerce City refinery—in Rutinel’s own state House district—against standards in California, Texas and Indiana and found multiple areas where Colorado’s current permits fall short.
**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|

Celebrate America’s 250th and Colorado’s 150th with with 2000+ patriots: two unforgettable days of speakers, action, community, and FUN for the whole family at the Douglas County Fairgrounds.
_America only turns 250 once. Colorado only turns 150 once._
Secure your tickets now and be part of it.
[SEE YOU THERE!](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
|
---
**[Big business taxes, small family credits, and a permanent tax on overtime](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY SHAINA COLE, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* **Big business tax hikes advance at the Capitol:** A four-bill package moving through the Colorado legislature would raise taxes on corporations, limit business deductions, and permanently require overtime pay to be taxed at the state level — even after Congress made overtime federally tax-deductible.
* **Supporters say families need permanent relief:** Democrats backing the bills argue the new revenue would fund an expanded Family Affordability Credit for lower-income parents, though projected benefits are modest compared to Colorado’s rising childcare and living costs.
* **Business leaders warn jobs and investment could leave Colorado:** Opponents testified the package could drive up prices, discourage hiring, and push employers to relocate, noting nearly 100 companies have already left the state since 2019.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---

The only way we can continue to spread truth is with your support!
[DONATE TO ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
|
---
**[As EEOC complaints climb, former federal official teaches Colorado workers their rights](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY JEN SCHUMANN, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* **Former EEOC official launches free workplace rights workshops:** Patty McMahon, a former Denver EEOC public affairs officer and current congressional candidate, is hosting public sessions across Colorado teaching workers how to recognize and respond to workplace discrimination and harassment.
* **Congressional harassment payouts draw renewed scrutiny:** The workshops come as Rep. Nancy Mace publicized subpoenaed records showing more than $300,000 in taxpayer-funded harassment settlements tied to former House members, reviving concerns about transparency and accountability in Congress.
* **EEOC complaints remain high as staffing hits historic lows:** The article notes the EEOC entered the fiscal year with its smallest workforce in decades while still handling more than 88,000 discrimination complaints annually, raising concerns about whether workers can get timely help.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**ONLY ON ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE ⤵️ **
**[You’ve been praying all along — you just didn’t know it](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)****BY DRAKE HUNTER | COMMENTARY | MAY 7** _Prayer sometimes gets a bad reputation for being formal. Folded hands, bowed heads, the right words in the right order. But walk into any coffee shop on any morning and listen carefully — and you’ll hear it everywhere. And once a year, a whole nation does exactly that — together._ __
**[Colorado loses businesses at one of nation’s highest rates, new report finds](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)****BY JEN SCHUMANN | STATE | MAY 6** _Colorado residents have spent years watching prices climb while business groups warn that operating in the state is becoming harder. A new report adds another layer of data to those concerns._
__

**[Transparency for All, Not Just Some](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)****BY REP. DUSTY JOHNSON | COMMENTARY | MAY 6** _Coloradans deserve a government that operates in the open. They deserve to know who is influencing their laws, how those decisions are being shaped, and how taxpayer dollars are being used in that process. That is exactly why I am proud to sponsor SB26-147._

**Feel like you have a unique story, commentary or tip to share?** Email [submit@rockymountainvoice.com](mailto:submit@rockymountainvoice.com).

name: Tom Fitton
subject: The End of Race-Based Gerrymandering?
body:
The Supreme Court has issued a major 6-3 decision which effectively prohibits the use of race to create “majority-minority” congressional districts: This is a great decision for democracy and affirms that the U.S. Constitution requires government to be color-blind in its decision-making.
| [ ](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=81365&L=14409&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9ZGVwbG95ZXImdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fY29udGVudD1BTWpjd09EazVOVFElM0QmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPU1heSZ1dG1fdGVybT1Ob24tRG9ub3Jz&hash=cbf44e67f3ede953fe8e284608b1050d98304e9f4df39ddcd4fb05803b508a8c)
---
Dear Fellow American, The **Supreme Court** has issued a _major 6-3 decision_ which effectively _prohibits_ the use of race to create "majority-minority" congressional districts: **This is a great decision for democracy and affirms that the U.S. Constitution requires government to be color-blind in its decision-making.** | [HELP JUDICIAL WATCH FIGHT
RACE-BASED GERRYMANDERING ](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=81365&L=37724&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9uYXRlL25kZS8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUFNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249TWF5JnV0bV90ZXJtPU5vbi1Eb25vcnM=&hash=68b0847428117e51ab31039e4536c339c16f4773136bac0bfa7930b30eeb998b)
**Judicial Watch** was proud to partner with the Allied Educational Foundation (AEF) in filing a key _amici_ brief (friend of the court) in support of this historic decision. Together, we argued: _Racial gerrymandering, like all "[r]acial classifications of any sort" cause "lasting harm to our society" because "[t]hey reinforce the belief, held by too many for too much of our history, that individuals should be judged by the color of their skin."_ _" There should be no question that race-based division...is a violation of the Equal Protection Clause"_ In his concurring opinion, Justice Thomas agreed stating: _" Blacks [we]re drawn into 'black districts' and given 'black representatives'... That interpretation rendered (Section 2) "repugnant to any nation that strives for the ideal of a color-blind Constitution."_ **This landmark ruling puts an end to the egregious racial segregation of voters...but now it must be enforced.** _Judicial Watch stands ready_ to do our part to enforce this decision and defend equal protection under the law. But these fights will require financial muscle. | [HELP US ENFORCE THIS RULING ](https://myjw.pr.judicialwatch.org/link.php?AGENCY=jw&M=27089954&N=81365&L=37724&F=H&drurl=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuanVkaWNpYWx3YXRjaC5vcmcvZG9uYXRlL25kZS8/dXRtX3NvdXJjZT1kZXBsb3llciZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWVtYWlsJnV0bV9jb250ZW50PUFNamN3T0RrNU5UUSUzRCZ1dG1fY2FtcGFpZ249TWF5JnV0bV90ZXJtPU5vbi1Eb25vcnM=&hash=68b0847428117e51ab31039e4536c339c16f4773136bac0bfa7930b30eeb998b)
This is not theoretical for Judicial Watch. **We know how to fight back (and win) against illegal gerrymandering.** It was Judicial Watch's lawsuit which resulted in Maryland's 2021 congressional redistricting plan being struck down as violating state law. As the years went on, the trauma only grew deeper. To survive, she turned to addiction \- the only way to numb the pain. The only way to keep going. She even had children with one of the men who trafficked her. Another chain and reason it felt impossible to escape. For years, she lived in fear. No way out. | Peter,

I won’t mince words: **ICE has been terrorizing American communities.**

Over the past few months, we’ve seen what happens when a federal law enforcement agency is allowed to act without accountability — masked agents rampaging through our streets, families ripped apart, and hardworking people living in fear in their own communities.

We don’t deserve to continue like this. That’s exactly why I’m running for Congress. To take this fight to Washington and hold ICE accountable for its abuses while protecting Michigan families.

**Here in Michigan, I’ve stood shoulder-to-shoulder with local officials, clergy, and neighbors to demand ICE out of Oakland County and metro Detroit.**

name: Tom Perriello
subject: Failure Is Not An Option
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY TOM PERRIELLO FOR CONGRESS
body:
